children.title: Pairwise Comparison Oracles
children.top_down_role: Relative objective information for pairs of queried alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Comparison Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact ordinal feedback for two queried objective points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\). The exact pairwise comparison oracle is the map \(\mathcal C_f:X\times X\to\{-1,0,1\}\) defined by \[\mathcal C_f(x,y)=\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(f(x)-f(y)\bigr).\] Thus a negative, zero, or positive response means respectively that \(f(x)<f(y)\), \(f(x)=f(y)\), or \(f(x)>f(y)\). The response is invariant under replacing \(f\) by \(\phi\circ f\) for any strictly increasing function \(\phi\), so calibrated objective magnitudes are not revealed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given two points, the oracle reports which has lower objective value, or reports equality, without revealing either numerical value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_f(x,y)=\operatorname{sgn}(f(x)-f(y))\) for every \((x,y)\in X^2\).

notation.meaning: sign map with values minus one, zero, and one

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the comparison-oracle definition or invariance property.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign-of-difference definition fits an exact pairwise comparison oracle, but no source is supplied. The invariance clause also fails to specify the domain and codomain of the strictly increasing map and therefore needs sourced, explicit formulation.

children.title: Multiway Ranking Oracles
children.top_down_role: Ordering information for collections of queried alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiway Ranking Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact ordinal feedback for a finite batch of queried points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \((x_1,\ldots,x_k)\in X^k\) with \(k\geq2\). An exact multiway ranking oracle returns the total preorder \(\preceq_f\) on \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\) satisfying \[i\preceq_f j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x_i)\leq f(x_j).\] Equivalently, it may return an ordered partition of the indices into equal-value classes arranged by increasing objective value. It reveals all within-batch ordinal relations but not the numerical values \(f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite batch, the oracle orders the points by objective value, grouping ties, while withholding calibrated values.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued.
The query batch has finite size \(k\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The response encodes exactly the relations \(i\preceq_f j\iff f(x_i)\leq f(x_j)\).

notation.meaning: objective-induced total preorder on batch indices

review_flags: No supplied source defines the batch-ranking oracle convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The total-preorder representation is mathematically coherent and fits the multiway-ranking leaf, but the finite-batch oracle convention and its exact information content have no supporting source locator.

children.title: Ties, Incomparability, or Abstention
children.top_down_role: Response regimes permitting unresolved order relations or withheld comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Ties, Incomparability, or Abstention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents generalized ordinal feedback as a set-valued relation-valued response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a query domain and let \(L=\{\prec,\sim,\succ,\parallel,?\}\), denoting strict preference, tie, reverse strict preference, incomparability, and abstention. A generalized ordinal oracle is a map \(\mathcal R:X\times X\to2^L\setminus\{\varnothing\}\). Exact responses satisfy \(\mathcal R(x,y)=\{\prec\}\) when \(f(x)<f(y)\), \(\mathcal R(x,y)=\{\sim\}\) when \(f(x)=f(y)\), and \(\mathcal R(x,y)=\{\succ\}\) when \(f(x)>f(y)\). The symbols \(\parallel\) and \(?\) respectively record a modeled absence of comparability and a refusal to decide; neither may be interpreted as equality without an additional oracle assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized ordinal feedback distinguishes equality, modeled incomparability, and refusal to answer; these outcomes are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) governs exact comparable responses.
The oracle model declares when incomparability or abstention is admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Responses \(\sim\), \(\parallel\), and \(?\) have distinct semantics unless the oracle model explicitly identifies them.
review_flags: The admissible semantics of incomparability and abstention are model-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation is a suitable content kind for this leaf, but the set-valued response space permits combinations whose semantics are not defined. Incomparability and abstention are model-dependent and require a source specifying admissible outputs and their interpretation.

children.title: Categorical Test Oracle Family
children.top_down_role: Categorical information relative to a prescribed test or level.

children.title: Sign Oracles
children.top_down_role: Categorical response information indicating the sign of a queried quantity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses sign feedback for a real-valued objective relative to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\). The exact sign oracle for \(f\) is the categorical map \(\mathcal S_f:X\to\{-1,0,1\}\) defined by \[\mathcal S_f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(f(x)).\] Its three responses certify respectively \(f(x)<0\), \(f(x)=0\), and \(f(x)>0\). The oracle does not reveal \(|f(x)|\); hence objectives having the same pointwise sign pattern induce identical sign-oracle transcripts for every adaptive querying algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point, the oracle reports whether the objective is negative, zero, or positive, but not its magnitude.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(f(x))\) for every \(x\in X\).
review_flags: The path does not establish whether sign applies to values, differences, or directional derivatives.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula correctly defines sign feedback for objective values relative to zero, but the immutable path alone does not distinguish this sense from signs of differences, derivatives, or directional derivatives. A source fixing the intended oracle convention is required.

children.title: Level-Test Oracles
children.top_down_role: Categorical information relative to a prescribed objective or operator level.

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Test Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a fixed, model-specified objective level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and fix a level \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) as part of the oracle specification. The exact level-test oracle is \(\mathcal L_{f,\alpha}:X\to\{0,1\}\) defined by \[\mathcal L_{f,\alpha}(x)=\mathbf 1_{\{f(x)\leq\alpha\}}.\] Thus the response decides membership of \(x\) in the sublevel set \(\{z\in X:f(z)\leq\alpha\}\). The queried point is variable, but the level \(\alpha\) is fixed and is not selected separately on each query.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed model-specified level, the oracle reports whether a queried point lies in the corresponding objective sublevel set.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued.
\(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) is fixed by the oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_{f,\alpha}(x)=1\iff f(x)\leq\alpha\).
review_flags: The distinction between level-test and threshold oracles is not fixed by supplied evidence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-level membership test is coherent and definition is the right content kind, but no evidence establishes that this taxonomy reserves “level-test” for a model-fixed level rather than a query-selected level.

children.title: Threshold Oracles
children.top_down_role: Categorical information indicating whether a queried quantity crosses a specified threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a query-selected threshold for binary objective-value testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\). The exact threshold oracle is the map \(\mathcal T_f:X\times\mathbb R\to\{0,1\}\) defined by \[\mathcal T_f(x,\tau)=\mathbf 1_{\{f(x)\leq\tau\}}.\] Both the point \(x\) and threshold \(\tau\) are supplied by the querying algorithm. Consequently, repeated threshold queries at a fixed point can bracket \(f(x)\); for example, responses at \(a<b\) certify \(a<f(x)\leq b\) when \(\mathcal T_f(x,a)=0\) and \(\mathcal T_f(x,b)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm supplies a point and threshold, and the oracle reports whether the objective value is at most that threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued.
Every real threshold \(\tau\) is admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_f(x,\tau)=1\iff f(x)\leq\tau\).
review_flags: The query-selected interpretation needs a source distinguishing it from fixed level tests.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The query-selected binary threshold definition and bracketing example are mathematically correct, but the distinction from the sibling fixed level-test oracle is taxonomy-specific and unsupported by a source locator.

children.title: Value–Gradient Oracles
children.top_down_role: Bundled objective-value and gradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Value–Gradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order oracle for differentiable real-valued objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, and let \(Q\subseteq U\) be the set of admissible query points. A value–gradient oracle for \(f\) on \(Q\) is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{f,\nabla f}:Q\to\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{f,\nabla f}(x)=(f(x),\nabla f(x))
\]
for every \(x\in Q\). One oracle call therefore returns the objective value and the complete first-order affine model \(y\mapsto f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\) at the queried point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible query point, the oracle deterministically returns both the objective value and the full gradient, and hence the objective's affine first-order model there.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(Q\subseteq U\).
\(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{f,\nabla f}(x)=(f(x),\nabla f(x))\) for every \(x\in Q\).

notation.meaning: gradient of the objective at the query point

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Only Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic access to gradients without an accompanying value response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, and let \(Q\subseteq U\) be the set of admissible query points. A gradient-only oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{\nabla f}:Q\to\mathbb{R}^n\) such that
\[
\mathcal{O}_{\nabla f}(x)=\nabla f(x)
\]
for every \(x\in Q\). Its response has no objective-value component \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible query point, the oracle returns the full gradient but does not bundle the corresponding objective value with its response.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(Q\subseteq U\).
\(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\nabla f}(x)=\nabla f(x)\) for every \(x\in Q\), with no value component in the response.

notation.meaning: gradient returned at the query point

children.title: Value–Subgradient Oracles
children.top_down_role: Bundled objective-value and selected subgradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Value–Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order oracle for finite convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(Q\subseteq X\) satisfy \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in Q\), where the subdifferential is taken relative to \(X\). A value–subgradient oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{f,\partial f}:Q\to\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{f,\partial f}(x)=(f(x),g_x),\qquad g_x\in\partial f(x),
\]
for every \(x\in Q\). Equivalently, the returned vector satisfies \(f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\) for every \(y\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible query point, the oracle returns the objective value and one deterministically selected subgradient defining a globally valid affine lower support on the convex domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite and convex.
\(Q\subseteq X\) and \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{f,\partial f}(x)=(f(x),g_x)\) with \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\) for every \(x\in Q\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential relative to the domain X
subgradient selected and returned by the oracle

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Selection Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection from a possibly set-valued convex subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(Q\subseteq X\) satisfy \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in Q\), where the subdifferential is taken relative to \(X\). A subgradient-selection oracle is a single-valued deterministic mapping \(S_f:Q\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[
S_f(x)\in\partial f(x)
\]
for every \(x\in Q\). When \(\partial f(x)\) contains multiple vectors, the oracle selects which valid subgradient is returned; no objective-value response is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible query point, the oracle deterministically chooses and returns one member of the convex subdifferential; when several subgradients exist, the querying algorithm does not control that choice.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex.
\(Q\subseteq X\) and \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_f(x)\in\partial f(x)\) for every \(x\in Q\).

notation.meaning: set of convex subgradients relative to X at the query point

children.title: Partial Derivative Access Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward finite-difference formula for Hessian entries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-value approximation of mixed second partial derivatives and its evaluation requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) admit a Taylor expansion at \(x\) with a third-order remainder, and let \(e_i\) denote the \(i\)-th coordinate vector. For \(i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and sufficiently small \(\epsilon\ne0\), \[\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x)=\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i+\epsilon e_j)-f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x+\epsilon e_j)+f(x)}{\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon).\] Computing all distinct Hessian entries this way uses \(n(n+1)/2\) pair-shift points and \(n\) single-coordinate shift points, excluding the reusable value \(f(x)\); evaluations corresponding to Hessian entries known to be zero may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the required Taylor expansion is valid, each mixed Hessian entry can be approximated from four function values by a forward coordinate-difference formula with first-order truncation error. All distinct entries require n(n+1)/2 pair-shift evaluations and n single-coordinate-shift evaluations, apart from the reusable baseline value; known structural zeros may be skipped.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}
f\text{ admits the required Taylor expansion with third-order remainder near }x
i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}
\epsilon\ne0\text{ is sufficiently small}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x)=\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i+\epsilon e_j)-f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x+\epsilon e_j)+f(x)}{\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse-Mode Adjoint Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-mode differentiation of a scalar output represented by a computational graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=x_N be the scalar output of a differentiable directed acyclic computational graph. After a forward evaluation has stored the required intermediate values and local arc derivatives \partial x_j/\partial x_i, initialize \bar{x}_N=1 and \bar{x}_i=0 for i\ne N. Process nodes from children to parents and accumulate \[\bar{x}_i\mathrel{+}=\bar{x}_j\frac{\partial x_j}{\partial x_i}\] for every arc i\to j. Once all child contributions have arrived, \[\bar{x}_i=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}=\sum_{j\text{ child of }i}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}\frac{\partial x_j}{\partial x_i}.\] The adjoints at the independent input nodes are the components of \nabla f.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation first evaluates the function and stores the local derivative data, then propagates adjoints backward from the scalar output. Initializing the output adjoint to one and accumulating each child's contribution gives the partial derivative of the output with respect to every intermediate and input variable; the input adjoints form the gradient.
assumptions_latex: f=x_N\in\mathbb{R}\text{ is the scalar output of a finite differentiable computational graph}
\text{The forward sweep supplies the required intermediate values and local derivatives }\partial x_j/\partial x_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar{x}_i=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}\text{ after all child contributions are accumulated, and }(\bar{x}_1,\ldots,\bar{x}_n)^T=\nabla f(x)\text{ for the independent inputs.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward and Central Finite-Difference Gradient Formulas
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate finite differences under smoothness and a stated absolute function-evaluation error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, let $\epsilon>0$, and suppose the required perturbations remain in the region of interest. If $f\in C^2$ and $\|\nabla^2f\|\le L$, then for each $i$, $$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)=\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x)}{\epsilon}+\delta_{\epsilon,i},\qquad |\delta_{\epsilon,i}|\le\frac L2\epsilon.$$ Reusing $f(x)$, all forward differences require evaluations at $n+1$ points. If $|\operatorname{comp}(f(y))-f(y)|\le\mathbf uL_f$, the componentwise forward-error bound is $$\frac L2\epsilon+\frac{2\mathbf uL_f}{\epsilon}.$$ For $L>0$, this bound is minimized at $\epsilon^2=4L_f\mathbf u/L$; under the stated well-scaled interpretation this motivates $\epsilon\approx\sqrt{\mathbf u}$ and error of order $\sqrt{\mathbf u}$. If $\nabla^2f$ is Lipschitz continuous, the central quotient $$\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x-\epsilon e_i)}{2\epsilon}$$ has truncation error $O(\epsilon^2)$. The described full-gradient procedure counts $2n+1$ points including $x$. Under the analogous roundoff model, balancing $O(\epsilon^2)$ truncation against $O(\mathbf u/\epsilon)$ evaluation error gives $\epsilon\approx\mathbf u^{1/3}$ and error of order $\mathbf u^{2/3}$ in a well-scaled problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a bounded Hessian, a forward coordinate difference has truncation error at most L epsilon over two, and the full forward-difference gradient uses n+1 points. Under the stated absolute evaluation-error model, its error is bounded by L epsilon/2 plus 2uLf/epsilon and is balanced at epsilon squared equal to 4Lf u/L. Lipschitz continuity of the Hessian gives quadratic truncation error for central differences; balancing this error with roundoff gives the familiar cube-root step and two-thirds-power error in a well-scaled problem.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R
\epsilon>0
x\pm\epsilon e_i\text{ lie in the region of interest when used}
f\in C^2\text{ and }\|\nabla^2f\|\le L\text{ for the forward truncation bound}
|\operatorname{comp}(f(y))-f(y)|\le\mathbf uL_f\text{ for the roundoff bounds}
L>0\text{ for the displayed minimizing step}
\nabla^2f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous for the }O(\epsilon^2)\text{ central truncation bound}
\text{the }\sqrt{\mathbf u}\text{ and }\mathbf u^{1/3}\text{ simplifications assume suitable scaling}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E_{\mathrm{fwd},i}|\le\frac L2\epsilon+\frac{2\mathbf uL_f}{\epsilon},\quad \epsilon_{\mathrm{fwd}}^2=\frac{4L_f\mathbf u}{L};\qquad E_{\mathrm{ctr},i}=O(\epsilon^2),\quad \epsilon_{\mathrm{ctr}}\approx\mathbf u^{1/3}\ \text{under the stated scaling model}

children.title: Directional-Derivative Oracles
children.top_down_role: First-order information restricted to queried directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Derivative Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic access to one-sided directional derivatives along queried directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(A\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}^n\) be a set of admissible point-direction pairs such that, for every \((x,d)\in A\), \(x+td\in X\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\) and the following limit exists finitely. A directional-derivative oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{f'}:A\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{f'}(x,d)=f'(x;d):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{f(x+td)-f(x)}{t}
\]
for every \((x,d)\in A\). A call reveals this scalar derivative only in the queried direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given an admissible point-direction pair, the oracle returns the finite scalar one-sided directional derivative in that direction, not an entire gradient vector.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(A\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}^n\) is the set of admissible point-direction pairs.
For every \((x,d)\in A\), the displayed one-sided limit is well-defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{f'}(x,d)=f'(x;d)\) for every \((x,d)\in A\).

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative of the objective at x along d

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian–Vector Product Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free forward-mode derivative access for differentiable vector mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable. A Jacobian–vector product oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{Jv}:X\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{Jv}(x,v)=J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]
\]
for each admissible point-direction pair \((x,v)\). The oracle returns the action of the Jacobian on \(v\) without requiring that the matrix \(J_F(x)\) itself be formed or exposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a point and input-space direction, the oracle returns the mapping's directional linearization, computed as a Jacobian–vector product without exposing the full Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable at every admissible query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{Jv}(x,v)=J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian matrix of the vector-valued mapping at the query point
Fréchet derivative applied to the queried direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Difference Jacobian Products and Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward directional differencing for a vector mapping, with dense and structurally compressed Jacobian construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ have Jacobian $J$, and suppose $J$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L$ in the region of interest. Then $$\|r(x+q)-r(x)-J(x)q\|\le\frac L2\|q\|^2.$$ Setting $q=\epsilon p$ gives, for $\epsilon\ne0$, $$\left\|\frac{r(x+\epsilon p)-r(x)}{\epsilon}-J(x)p\right\|\le\frac L2|\epsilon|\|p\|^2.$$ Thus the forward directional approximation has $O(|\epsilon|)$ error for fixed $p$. Taking $p=e_i$ estimates the $i$th column, and reusing $r(x)$ yields a full columnwise estimate from $n+1$ evaluations of $r$. When a compatible Jacobian sparsity structure is known, suitable perturbations may estimate several structurally independent columns simultaneously and reduce the evaluation count. A two-sided directional analogue can also be formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector function with a Lipschitz Jacobian, a forward directional difference approximates a Jacobian–vector product with first-order error in the step for a fixed direction. Coordinate directions recover individual columns, so a dense columnwise estimate uses n+1 function evaluations when the base value is reused. A known compatible sparsity pattern can allow several columns to be estimated simultaneously, reducing the evaluation count.
assumptions_latex: r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m
\|J(y)-J(z)\|\le L\|y-z\|\text{ in the region of interest}
\epsilon\ne0
x+\epsilon p\text{ lies in the region of interest}
p\text{ is fixed for the }O(|\epsilon|)\text{ conclusion}
\text{simultaneous column recovery requires a compatible known sparsity structure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\|\frac{r(x+\epsilon p)-r(x)}{\epsilon}-J(x)p\right\|\le\frac L2|\epsilon|\|p\|^2=O(|\epsilon|)\quad\text{for fixed }p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward and Reverse Automatic Differentiation of Vector Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative products and full-Jacobian recovery for a differentiable vector mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m be differentiable with Jacobian J(x). For any seed p\in\mathbb{R}^n, one forward-mode sweep returns \[D_pr(x)=J(x)p.\] For any seed q\in\mathbb{R}^m, applying reverse mode to the scalar r(x)^Tq returns \[\nabla(r(x)^Tq)=J(x)^Tq.\] Coordinate seeds p=e_1,\ldots,e_n recover all columns of J, while q=e_1,\ldots,e_m recover all rows. When the sparsity pattern is known, graph-coloring seed compression can reduce the number of sweeps; forward and reverse seeds may also be combined to recover complementary columns and rows. The arithmetic factor is approximately the number of forward seeds and at most five times the number of reverse seeds relative to evaluating r alone. A single forward sweep computes a required product J(x)p at cost comparable to one evaluation of r.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector function, forward-mode automatic differentiation computes a Jacobian–vector product, while reverse mode applied to a seeded scalar combination of outputs computes a Jacobian-transpose–vector product. Unit seeds recover the full Jacobian; sparsity coloring and mixed forward/reverse sweeps can reduce the number of passes. A single Jp product costs about one function evaluation, and reverse recovery has at most about five function-evaluation equivalents per seed in the stated model.
assumptions_latex: r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is differentiable at }x
J(x)=Dr(x)
p\in\mathbb{R}^n,\quad q\in\mathbb{R}^m
\text{Coloring compression additionally assumes a known exploitable sparsity pattern of }J(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{forward}(p)=J(x)p,\qquad \operatorname{reverse}(q)=J(x)^Tq,\quad\text{with unit or compressed seeds recovering the required Jacobian information.}

children.title: Adjoint-Jacobian Product Oracles
children.top_down_role: Matrix-free reverse linearized access associated with scalarizations or adjoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Jacobian Product Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free reverse-mode derivative access for differentiable vector mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable. An adjoint-Jacobian product oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{J^*u}:X\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{J^*u}(x,u)=J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}u=\nabla_x\langle u,F(x)\rangle
\]
for every admissible \((x,u)\). It returns the adjoint action associated with the scalarization \(\langle u,F(\cdot)\rangle\) without exposing the full Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a point and output-space covector, the oracle returns the transposed-Jacobian product, equivalently the gradient of the corresponding scalarization, without exposing the Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable at every admissible query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{J^*u}(x,u)=J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}u=\nabla_x\langle u,F(x)\rangle\).

notation.meaning: adjoint-Jacobian action on the output-space covector

children.title: Affine Support-Model Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Support-Model Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane access for finite convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. An affine support-model oracle returns, at each admissible \(x\in X\), coefficients \((a_x,g_x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\) defining \(m_x(y)=a_x+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\) such that
\[
m_x(y)\leq f(y)\quad\text{for every }y\in X,
\qquad m_x(x)=f(x).
\]
Thus \(a_x=f(x)\) and \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\), and the returned model supplies a valid supporting cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a query point, the oracle returns an affine function touching the convex objective there and globally underestimating it, thereby providing a supporting cut.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite and convex, with a subgradient at each admissible query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x(x)=f(x)\) and \(m_x(y)\leq f(y)\) for all \(y\in X\).

notation.meaning: affine support model returned at the query point
slope of the supporting affine model

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Local-Model Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-model access augmented by a declared regularizer or geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\). A regularized local-model oracle queried at \(x\in X\) returns a model \(m_x:X\to\mathbb{R}\), a regularizer \(R_x:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and a parameter \(\lambda_x>0\). The associated regularized model is
\[
M_x(y)=m_x(y)+\lambda_x R_x(y),
\]
where \(R_x(x)=0\), \(R_x(y)\geq0\), and the response declares the geometry and domain used by \(R_x\). The oracle output is the complete data needed to evaluate or minimize \(M_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns a local objective model together with a nonnegative, centered regularizer, its weight, and the geometry or domain needed to use the regularized model.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in X\).
\(R_x(x)=0\) and \(R_x(y)\geq0\) for every \(y\in X\).
\(\lambda_x>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned data define \(M_x(y)=m_x(y)+\lambda_xR_x(y)\) on the declared domain.

notation.meaning: unregularized local model at the query point

children.title: Model-Fidelity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Information qualifying the region, order, or accuracy in which a returned model is valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Fidelity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative interface declaring where and how accurately a local model represents an objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and let \(m_x:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be a model returned at \(x\in X\). A model-fidelity interface consists of a declared set \(D_x\subseteq X\), an order \(p>0\), and a constant \(\kappa_x\geq0\) for which
\[
|f(y)-m_x(y)|\leq\kappa_x\|y-x\|^p\qquad\text{for every }y\in D_x.
\]
The interface may equivalently declare a radius \(\Delta_x\geq0\) with \(D_x=\{y\in X:\|y-x\|\leq\Delta_x\}\); outside \(D_x\), no fidelity guarantee is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface reports a validity region and an explicit error order and constant bounding the discrepancy between the returned model and the true objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(m_x:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(D_x\subseteq X\), \(p>0\), and \(\kappa_x\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(y)-m_x(y)|\leq\kappa_x\|y-x\|^p\) for all \(y\in D_x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Lipschitz problem class and deterministic linear-span oracle methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition for unconstrained convex nonsmooth oracle complexity in Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be convex, x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, and R,M>0. The class \mathcal{P}(x_0,R,M) consists of pairs (f,x^*) such that x^*\in\arg\min f, \|x_0-x^*\|\le R, and |f(x)-f(y)|\le M\|x-y\| for all x,y\in B_2(x^*,R). Writing f^*=f(x^*), an \epsilon-approximate solution, for \epsilon\ge0, is any \bar x with f(\bar x)-f^*\le\epsilon. A first-order black-box oracle returns (f(\hat x),g(\hat x)) with g(\hat x)\in\partial f(\hat x). A deterministic linear-span method starting from x_0 must satisfy x_k\in x_0+\operatorname{Lin}\{g(x_0),\ldots,g(x_{k-1})\} for every k\ge1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The problem class contains convex functions with a minimizer within distance R of the starting point and Lipschitz constant M on the radius-R ball around that minimizer. Approximate solutions are measured by objective gap. The exact first-order oracle returns a value and subgradient, and each deterministic iterate must lie in the affine span generated by all previously returned subgradients.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex}
x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n
\epsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (f,x^*)\in\mathcal{P}(x_0,R,M),\quad f(\bar x)-f^*\le\epsilon,\quad g(\hat x)\in\partial f(\hat x),\quad x_k\in x_0+\operatorname{Lin}\{g(x_0),\ldots,g(x_{k-1})\}\ \forall k\ge1

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic full-Hessian access for twice differentiable scalar objectives, optionally bundled with lower-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice Fréchet differentiable, and let \(Q\subseteq U\) be the set of admissible query points. A full second-order oracle for \(f\) is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}^{(2)}_f:Q\to\mathbb{S}^n\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}^{(2)}_f(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)
\]
for every \(x\in Q\). A convention may bundle \(f(x)\) and \(\nabla f(x)\) with this Hessian response; when it does, the returned data determine the quadratic Taylor model \(q_x(d)=f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,\nabla^2 f(x)d\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible query point, a full second-order oracle returns the complete Hessian. Some access conventions additionally bundle the objective value and gradient, in which case the response determines the quadratic Taylor model.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(Q\subseteq U\).
\(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}^{(2)}_f(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)\) for every \(x\in Q\).

notation.meaning: space of real symmetric matrices of order n
Hessian of the objective at the query point
quadratic Taylor model available when lower-order data are bundled

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian–Vector Product Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free directional curvature access for twice differentiable scalar objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice Fréchet differentiable, and let \(A\subseteq U\times\mathbb{R}^n\) be the set of admissible point-direction queries. A Hessian–vector product oracle is a deterministic mapping \(\mathcal{O}_{Hv}:A\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal{O}_{Hv}(x,v)=\nabla^2 f(x)v=D(\nabla f)(x)[v]
\]
for every \((x,v)\in A\). The response gives the directional change of the gradient along \(v\) without requiring the full Hessian matrix to be formed or returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given an admissible point and direction, the oracle returns the Hessian applied to that direction, exposing directional curvature without returning the full Hessian matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open.
\(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice Fréchet differentiable.
\(A\subseteq U\times\mathbb{R}^n\) is the set of admissible point-direction queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{Hv}(x,v)=\nabla^2 f(x)v=D(\nabla f)(x)[v]\) for every \((x,v)\in A\).

notation.meaning: Hessian action on the queried direction

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Derivative Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic local access to derivatives of a fixed order exceeding two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be an open subset of a Banach space \(X\), let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\), and fix an integer \(p\ge 3\). A higher-derivative oracle of order \(p\) is a mapping that, for every query \(x\in U\) at which \(f\) is \(p\)-times Fréchet differentiable, returns \(D^p f(x)\), or the derivative jet \((f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^p f(x))\). Here \(D^j f(x)\) is a continuous symmetric \(j\)-linear form on \(X^j\). An oracle call counts as one access independently of how the returned multilinear forms are subsequently represented or contracted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-p higher-derivative oracle returns the pth Fréchet derivative, or the complete derivative jet through order p, at each queried point.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq X\) is open and \(p\ge 3\).
\(f\) is \(p\)-times Fréchet differentiable at every admissible query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_p(x)=D^p f(x)\) or \(\mathcal{O}_p(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^p f(x))\).

notation.meaning: The jth Fréchet derivative, viewed as a continuous symmetric j-linear form.
The highest derivative order returned by the oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Value Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic absolute-error access to objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\delta:X\to[0,\infty)\) be a declared error budget. A deterministically inexact value oracle returns a scalar \(\widetilde f(x)\) at each query \(x\in X\) such that \[|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le \delta(x).\] The error may be chosen adversarially and may depend on the query history, provided the displayed bound holds for every returned value. Constant-accuracy access is the special case \(\delta(x)\equiv\delta\); exact value access is recovered when \(\delta\equiv0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact value oracle returns a deterministic approximation whose absolute deviation from the true objective value obeys a declared pointwise error budget.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite-valued.
\(\delta:X\to[0,\infty)\) is known to the oracle user.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le\delta(x)\) for every query \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: The approximate objective value returned at x.
The permitted absolute value error at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise absolute-error condition is precise and fits the leaf, but the record has no citation. In particular, the allowance for adversarial, history-dependent deterministic errors is a substantive oracle-model choice requiring source support.

children.title: Inexact First-Order Access
children.top_down_role: Gradient, subgradient, or support information with controlled error.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact First-Order Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex first-order access through an approximate value and an approximate supporting slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a normed space \(X\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. A deterministic \(\delta\)-inexact first-order oracle returns \((\widetilde f(x),g_x)\in\mathbb{R}\times X^*\) at each \(x\in C\) such that \[|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le\delta\quad\text{and}\quad f(y)\ge \widetilde f(x)+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle-\delta\quad\text{for all }y\in C.\] Thus \(g_x\) supplies an approximate supporting affine function. When \(f\) is differentiable, an alternative gradient-error specification is \(\|g_x-\nabla f(x)\|_*\le\delta_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns an approximate value and slope defining a globally valid affine lower model up to deterministic error; differentiable problems may instead bound gradient error.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex.
\(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le\delta\) and \(f(y)\ge\widetilde f(x)+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle-\delta\) for all \(y\in C\).

notation.meaning: The continuous dual of the normed space X.
The returned approximate subgradient or supporting slope.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative fidelity measured relative to the exact response norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to Y\) be the exact response map into a normed space \(Y\), and let \(\widetilde T(x)\) be the response returned at query \(x\in X\). For a prescribed \(\eta\in[0,1)\), relative-error access satisfies \[\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_Y\le \eta\|T(x)\|_Y\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Consequently, if \(T(x)=0\), the response must be exact at \(x\). The definition applies to scalar values, gradients, residuals, or other normed oracle outputs after the exact response map and norm have been declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative-error access bounds response error by a fixed fraction of the exact response magnitude and therefore requires exact output when that magnitude vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) maps into a normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_Y\le\eta\|T(x)\|_Y\) for all \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: The exact oracle response at x.
The inexact response returned at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-norm inequality and its zero-response consequence are correct, but no source is provided for adopting this particular exact-response-relative model as the meaning of the terminal container across scalar, gradient, residual, and other outputs.

children.title: Query-Scale-Dependent Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Response quality varying with the scale of the submitted query.

knowledge_statements.title: Query-Scale-Dependent Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fidelity controlled by an explicit scale attached to each query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to Y\) be an exact response map into a normed space, and let every query consist of a point-scale pair \((x,r)\in X\times(0,\infty)\). An oracle has query-scale-dependent fidelity with modulus \(\omega:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) when its response \(\widetilde T(x;r)\) satisfies \[\|\widetilde T(x;r)-T(x)\|_Y\le\omega(r)\] for every admissible \((x,r)\), where \(\omega\) is nondecreasing and \(\lim_{r\downarrow0}\omega(r)=0\). Thus decreasing the declared localization or resolution scale forces asymptotically exact responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point-scale query receives a response whose deterministic error is bounded by a modulus of the declared scale and vanishes as that scale tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) maps into a normed space.
\(\omega\) is nondecreasing and \(\omega(r)\to0\) as \(r\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde T(x;r)-T(x)\|_Y\le\omega(r)\) for every admissible \((x,r)\).

notation.meaning: The localization or resolution scale supplied with the query.
The error modulus as a function of query scale.
The response at point x and declared scale r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent proposed model, but the meaning of the query scale and the imposed monotone, vanishing modulus are not canonical across oracle frameworks. An authoritative source must establish that this formulation matches the intended terminal concept.

children.title: Geometry-Dependent Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Response quality varying with local geometric features of the instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Dependent Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error measured in norms selected by the local problem geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(T:X\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and associate each query \(x\) with a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_x\). Define \(\|u\|_{x}=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}H_xu}\) and its dual norm \(\|v\|_{x,*}=\sqrt{v^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}v}\). A vector-response oracle has geometry-dependent fidelity with budget \(\delta(x)\ge0\) if \[\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_{x,*}\le\delta(x)\quad\text{for every query }x.\] The matrices and budgets must be declared independently of the returned error, so the condition is verifiable in the specified local geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometry-dependent fidelity measures vector-response error in a declared local dual norm, allowing accuracy requirements to vary with the problem geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(H_x\) is symmetric positive definite at every query.
\(\delta(x)\ge0\) is declared independently of the response error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_{x,*}\le\delta(x)\) for every query \(x\).

notation.meaning: The positive-definite matrix defining the local geometry.
The dual norm induced by the inverse of H_x.
The permitted error in the local dual norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local dual-norm formula is internally consistent, but geometry-dependent fidelity could use primal norms, dual norms, Bregman geometry, or other local metrics depending on the response type. No source supports selecting this finite-dimensional SPD dual-norm specialization as the container's definition.

children.title: Magnitude-Dependent Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Response quality varying with the magnitude of the information being returned.

knowledge_statements.title: Magnitude-Dependent Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed absolute-relative error controlled by the exact response magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to Y\) be an exact response map into a normed space \(Y\). An oracle has magnitude-dependent fidelity with parameters \(a,b\ge0\) when every returned response \(\widetilde T(x)\) satisfies \[\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_Y\le a+b\|T(x)\|_Y\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] The constant \(a\) is an absolute error floor and \(b\|T(x)\|_Y\) scales with response magnitude. Pure absolute access has \(b=0\), while pure relative access has \(a=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Magnitude-dependent fidelity combines an absolute error floor with an error term proportional to the exact response magnitude.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) maps into a normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde T(x)-T(x)\|_Y\le a+b\|T(x)\|_Y\) for all \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: The exact response whose magnitude controls part of the error budget.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed absolute-relative inequality is mathematically precise and its special cases are correct, but no source is supplied for identifying it with magnitude-dependent oracle fidelity or for the chosen dependence on the exact rather than returned response magnitude.

children.title: Controllable-Accuracy Access
children.top_down_role: Interfaces coupling requested fidelity to the cost of a response.

knowledge_statements.title: Controllable-Accuracy Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle access parameterized by requested error and its declared computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to Y\) be an exact response map into a normed space. A controllable-accuracy oracle accepts a query \((x,\varepsilon)\in X\times(0,\infty)\), returns \(\widetilde T(x;\varepsilon)\), and guarantees \[\|\widetilde T(x;\varepsilon)-T(x)\|_Y\le\varepsilon.\] The access model also declares a nonincreasing cost function \(C:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty]\), where one such call consumes at most \(C(\varepsilon)\) elementary work units. An algorithm may select \(\varepsilon\) adaptively from previous responses; its total oracle cost is the sum of the costs of its calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The user requests an accuracy, the oracle meets that error tolerance, and the access model charges a declared accuracy-dependent cost.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) maps into a normed space.
\(C(\varepsilon)\) is nonincreasing as the requested tolerance increases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde T(x;\varepsilon)-T(x)\|_Y\le\varepsilon\) at cost at most \(C(\varepsilon)\) per call.

notation.meaning: The error tolerance requested by the algorithm.
The declared cost of meeting tolerance epsilon.
The response computed to the requested accuracy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accuracy-parameterized interface fits the leaf, but the declared upper-bound cost function, its monotonicity, adaptive tolerance selection, and additive total-cost convention are substantive access-model assumptions with no cited locator.

children.title: Stochastic Value Oracles
children.top_down_role: Random objective-value information at queried points.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased random objective values with a conditional variance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a query set and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\). A stochastic value oracle, queried at \(x\in X\), returns a random scalar \(F(x,\xi)\). Relative to the history \(\mathcal{H}\) before the call, an unbiased variance-bounded oracle satisfies \[\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)\mid\mathcal{H}]=f(x),\qquad \mathbb{E}[(F(x,\xi)-f(x))^2\mid\mathcal{H}]\le\sigma^2(x).\] The query \(x\) may be \(\mathcal{H}\)-measurable, while the new random seed is conditionally distributed according to the declared sampling mechanism. Biased stochastic value access requires a separate stated bias bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic value oracle returns a random objective estimate that is conditionally unbiased and has bounded conditional variance at the queried point.
assumptions_latex: The query \(x\) is measurable with respect to the pre-call history \(\mathcal H\).
\(F(x,\xi)\) has a finite conditional second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)\mid\mathcal H]=f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[(F(x,\xi)-f(x))^2\mid\mathcal H]\le\sigma^2(x)\).

notation.meaning: The random value returned at query x.
The information available before the oracle call.
The conditional variance bound at x.

children.title: Stochastic First-Order Oracles
children.top_down_role: Random gradient, subgradient, or bundled loss-and-gradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic First-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditionally unbiased random gradients or subgradients with bounded second moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space \(X\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. A stochastic first-order oracle queried at \(x\in C\) returns a random element \(G(x,\xi)\in X^*\) such that, conditional on the pre-call history \(\mathcal H\), \[\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)\mid\mathcal H]\in\partial f(x),\qquad \mathbb E[\|G(x,\xi)\|_*^2\mid\mathcal H]\le M^2.\] If \(f\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(x\), the first condition becomes \(\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)\mid\mathcal H]=Df(x)\), with \(Df(x)\in X^*\). A bundled oracle may additionally return a sampled loss whose conditional expectation equals \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic first-order oracle returns a random continuous linear functional whose conditional mean is a valid convex subgradient and whose conditional dual-norm second moment obeys a declared bound; it may also return an unbiased sampled loss.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty and convex, \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
The query \(x\) is measurable with respect to the pre-call history \(\mathcal H\).
\(G(x,\xi)\in X^*\) has a finite conditional second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)\mid\mathcal H]\in\partial f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G(x,\xi)\|_*^2\mid\mathcal H]\le M^2\).

notation.meaning: The continuous dual of the finite-dimensional normed space X.
The random first-order response in the dual space.
The convex subdifferential of f at x, a subset of the dual space.
The uniform conditional dual-norm second-moment bound.

children.title: Mini-Batch Oracles
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous local access to a declared number of random responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaged simultaneous access to a declared number of conditionally independent samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a base stochastic oracle return vectors \(G(x,\xi)\in Y\) at a query \(x\). For an integer batch size \(b\ge1\), a mini-batch oracle draws \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_b\) conditionally independently given the pre-call history and returns \[\overline G_b(x)=\frac1b\sum_{i=1}^b G(x,\xi_i).\] If each sample has conditional mean \(T(x)\) and conditional mean-square error at most \(\sigma^2\), then \(\mathbb E[\overline G_b(x)\mid\mathcal H]=T(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\overline G_b(x)-T(x)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal H]\le\sigma^2/b\) in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mini-batch oracle averages b conditionally independent responses at one query, preserving unbiasedness and reducing Euclidean mean-square error by a factor of b.
assumptions_latex: \(b\ge1\) is declared before the call.
The samples are conditionally independent with common conditional mean \(T(x)\).
Each sample has conditional Euclidean mean-square error at most \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\overline G_b(x)\mid\mathcal H]=T(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\overline G_b(x)-T(x)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal H]\le\sigma^2/b\).

notation.meaning: The number of random responses in the batch.
The common conditional mean of the base responses.

children.title: Simulation-Response Oracles
children.top_down_role: Local objective or constraint information available through stochastic simulation or experiment.

knowledge_statements.title: Simulation-Response Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle responses generated by a declared stochastic simulator or experiment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a query set, let \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\) be a measurable response space, and assign to each \(x\in X\) a probability kernel \(P_x\). A simulation-response oracle queried at \(x\) generates \(Z_x\sim P_x\) and returns a declared statistic \(S(x,Z_x)\). The optimization-relevant quantity is \[T(x)=\mathbb E_{Z\sim P_x}[S(x,Z)],\] whenever the expectation exists. Independent replication is obtained by drawing fresh samples from \(P_x\); common-random-number coupling or stateful simulation must instead be included explicitly in the oracle specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simulation-response oracle runs a declared experiment at the query and returns a statistic whose distribution and expectation define the accessible optimization information.
assumptions_latex: \(x\mapsto P_x\) is a probability kernel on \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\).
\(S(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and integrable under \(P_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_x\sim P_x\), the oracle returns \(S(x,Z_x)\), and \(T(x)=\mathbb E_{Z\sim P_x}[S(x,Z)]\).

notation.meaning: The simulator response distribution at query x.
The random experimental or simulated outcome.
The statistic returned by the oracle.

children.title: Fresh-Sample Access
children.top_down_role: Interfaces supplying newly drawn observations through successive interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Fresh-Sample Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online access in which every oracle call uses a newly drawn population observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)\), \((\mathcal X,\mathscr X)\), \((\mathcal U,\mathscr U)\), and \((\mathcal Y,\mathscr Y)\) be measurable spaces, and let \(P\) be a probability distribution on \(\mathcal Z\). Before call \(t\), let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the preceding transcript and the algorithmic randomness already used, and let the query \(x_t\in\mathcal X\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. A stochastic oracle has fresh-sample access if it draws \(Z_t\) with \(\mathcal L(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P\), draws auxiliary oracle randomness \(U_t\) independently of \(\sigma(\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_t)\), and returns \(Y_t=\Psi(x_t,Z_t,U_t)\) for a measurable map \(\Psi:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\times\mathcal U\to\mathcal Y\). The access model does not permit any later response to depend on \(Z_t\) except through information recorded in the transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each adaptive oracle call uses a new population draw that is independent of the preceding interaction, and the underlying observation cannot be queried again later except through information already recorded in the transcript.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)\), \((\mathcal X,\mathscr X)\), \((\mathcal U,\mathscr U)\), and \((\mathcal Y,\mathscr Y)\) are measurable spaces.
\(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and \(\mathcal L(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P\).
\(U_t\) is independent of \(\sigma(\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_t=\Psi(x_t,Z_t,U_t)\) uses a new observation at call \(t\), and later calls cannot access \(Z_t\) beyond its recorded transcript contribution.

notation.meaning: Information available before oracle call t.
Adaptively selected query at call t.
Fresh population observation used at call t.

children.title: Reusable-Dataset Access
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing a retained dataset for multiple computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable-Dataset Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-data access allowing repeated, adaptive interrogation of the same realized observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)\), \((\mathcal X,\mathscr X)\), \((\mathcal U,\mathscr U)\), and \((\mathcal Y,\mathscr Y)\) be measurable spaces, let \(P\) be a probability distribution on \(\mathcal Z\), and sample \(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\sim P^n\) once. An oracle has reusable-dataset access if, at each call \(t\), an adaptively selected query \(x_t\in\mathcal X\) and fresh auxiliary randomness \(U_t\in\mathcal U\) produce \(Y_t=\Psi_t(x_t,S,U_t)\in\mathcal Y\), where \(x_t\) and the measurable response rule \(\Psi_t\) may depend on the preceding transcript, and \(U_t\) is conditionally independent of \(S\) given that transcript. The same observation \(Z_i\) may influence arbitrarily many responses, subject to any separately declared query, privacy, or computational restrictions; the access model does not require a new independent observation at each call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed random dataset is sampled once and may be interrogated repeatedly by adaptively selected queries, with the same observations permitted to affect multiple responses.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)\), \((\mathcal X,\mathscr X)\), \((\mathcal U,\mathscr U)\), and \((\mathcal Y,\mathscr Y)\) are measurable spaces.
\(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\sim P^n\) is realized once and retained.
Queries and response rules may be selected adaptively from the preceding transcript.
\(U_t\) is conditionally independent of \(S\) given the preceding transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every call \(t\), \(Y_t=\Psi_t(x_t,S,U_t)\) may reuse any elements of the same retained dataset \(S\).

notation.meaning: Product law of n independent population observations.
Adaptively selected query at call t.

children.title: Observation-Reuse Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on retaining, revisiting, or recomputing from previously exposed observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Observation-Reuse Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript criterion separating fresh observations from data that remain available for later oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a transcript \(T_t=(x_1,Y_1,\ldots,x_t,Y_t)\), observation \(Z_i\) is reusable after call \(t\ge i\) precisely when some admissible future response kernel may depend on \(Z_i\) beyond its recorded contribution to \(T_t\): there exist an admissible \(s>t\), query \(x_s\), and datasets differing only at coordinate \(i\) for which the conditional laws of \(Y_s\) given \(T_t\) differ. If every admissible future-response law is conditionally invariant under such replacements, reuse of \(Z_i\) is prohibited beyond the transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An observation crosses the reuse boundary exactly when changing it can alter a later response after the current transcript is fixed.
assumptions_latex: Future queries and response kernels must belong to the declared access model.
Compared datasets differ only in the observation whose reuse is tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_i\) is nonreusable after \(T_t\) iff every admissible future conditional response law is invariant to replacing \(Z_i\) while holding \(T_t\) fixed.

notation.meaning: Observation being tested for future reuse.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional-law invariance is a standard operational criterion for whether hidden data can affect future interaction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed operational condition is plausible, but comparing conditional future-response laws while holding a transcript fixed requires a specified experiment, coupling or regular conditional distribution, and treatment of transcripts that have zero probability under a replaced dataset. These choices affect the claimed equivalence, so an authoritative source and precise model are required.

children.title: Empirical-Objective Access
children.top_down_role: Access to a finite empirical objective induced by reusable data.

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical-Objective Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle access to a finite-sum objective determined by one reusable sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\) be a fixed sample, and let each component loss \(\ell_i=\ell(\cdot;Z_i):\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be convex. Define \(F_S(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i(x)\). Empirical-objective access permits adaptive queries to declared information derived from this fixed finite sum. A value query returns \(F_S(x)\); a full first-order query returns some \(g\in\partial F_S(x)\), where \(\partial\) denotes the convex subdifferential; and, when component access is declared, a query \((x,i)\) may return \(\ell_i(x)\) or some \(g_i\in\partial\ell_i(x)\). Every reply concerns the same realized sample \(S\), so repeated replies need not be conditionally independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle exposes declared values or convex first-order information for a finite empirical objective built from one reusable sample; component information is available only when component access is explicitly included.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\) is fixed throughout the interaction.
Each \(\ell_i=\ell(\cdot;Z_i):\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
The available value, full first-order, and component query types are declared by the access model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accessible objective is \(F_S(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i(x)\), and every admitted response is derived from this same finite sum or one of its declared components.

notation.meaning: Empirical objective induced by the fixed sample S.
Component loss associated with observation i.
Convex subdifferential of the empirical objective at x.
A convex subgradient of component loss i at x.

children.title: Statistical-Query Access
children.top_down_role: Approximate population expectations obtained through bounded statistical queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical-Query Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate population-expectation access for bounded, adaptively selected query functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a distribution on \(\mathcal Z\), let \(\tau\ge0\), and let \(\Phi\) be a declared class of measurable functions \(\phi:\mathcal Z\to[-1,1]\). A tolerance-\(\tau\) statistical-query oracle accepts any adaptively chosen \(\phi_t\in\Phi\) and returns \(v_t\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\lvert v_t-\mathbb E_{Z\sim P}[\phi_t(Z)]\rvert\le\tau\). The oracle need not reveal observations or use a fixed dataset, and its admissible error may depend adversarially on the interaction while respecting the displayed bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each bounded query receives an approximation, within tolerance, to its population expectation; individual observations are not exposed.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\phi_t\in\Phi\) is measurable and takes values in \([-1,1]\).
Queries may depend on previous query-answer pairs.
The tolerance \(\tau\) is fixed or declared for each query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert v_t-\mathbb E_{Z\sim P}[\phi_t(Z)]\rvert\le\tau\) for every admitted query \(\phi_t\).
