children.title: Centered Responses
children.top_down_role: Stochastic information aligned with its designated population target.

knowledge_statements.title: Centered Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional unbiasedness of a stochastic first-order response relative to the query history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the interaction history before call \(t\), let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and let \(G_t\) be the stochastic response. The response is centered about a target mapping \(g:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d\) when \(G_t\) is conditionally integrable and \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=g(x_t)\) almost surely. Equivalently, the noise \(\xi_t=G_t-g(x_t)\) is a martingale difference: \(\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A response is centered when its conditional expectation, given the past, equals the intended first-order quantity at the current query.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
\(G_t\) is conditionally integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_t-g(x_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Information available before oracle call t.
Target first-order response at the current query.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional mean-zero noise is the standard centered stochastic-oracle condition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional mean-zero formulation is mathematically precise and condition is an appropriate kind for this response-bias class, but the record has no inspectable source locator. The standard-field rationale alone does not provide the requested citation-level support.

children.title: Biased Responses
children.top_down_role: Stochastic information carrying systematic displacement from its designated target.

knowledge_statements.title: Biased Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional response error with a nonzero predictable mean component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the filtration \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), a conditionally integrable response \(G_t\) to the adapted query \(x_t\) is biased relative to a target mapping \(g\) when its conditional bias \(b_t=\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]-g(x_t)\) is not almost surely zero. It admits the decomposition \(G_t=g(x_t)+b_t+\varepsilon_t\), where \(b_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) almost surely. A bounded-bias model additionally imposes \(\lVert b_t\rVert\le\beta_t\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic response is biased when its conditional mean differs from the target; the difference is its predictable bias.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
\(G_t\) is conditionally integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_t=\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]-g(x_t)\neq0\) with positive probability for at least one \(t\).

notation.meaning: Optional deterministic or predictable bias bound.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: decomposition into conditional bias and martingale-difference residual is standard
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-bias decomposition is standard, but no source is cited and the target mapping g is not locally assigned a domain and codomain. Source confirmation should also establish whether the intended leaf includes arbitrary bias, bounded predictable bias, or both.

children.title: Bias Detectability
children.top_down_role: Access distinctions based on whether systematic response displacement can be identified or bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias Detectability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform statistical distinguishability of centered and meaningfully biased oracle-response laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an access protocol and two classes of transcript laws: \(\mathcal P_0\), under which responses are centered, and \(\mathcal P_{1,\beta}\), under which the declared bias magnitude is at least \(\beta>0\). Bias is uniformly detectable if there exist transcript-based tests \(\delta_T\in\{0,1\}\) such that \(\sup_{P
automation\mathcal P_0}P(\delta_T=1)+\sup_{P
automation\mathcal P_{1,\beta}}P(\delta_T=0)\to0\) as \(T\to\infty\). It is undetectable under the protocol if the infimum of this total error over all tests stays bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias is detectable when transcript-based tests can uniformly separate centered oracles from oracles whose bias exceeds a fixed threshold.
assumptions_latex: The centered and biased transcript-law classes are specified under the same access protocol.
The alternative bias threshold satisfies \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Detectability holds exactly when a sequence of transcript tests has uniformly vanishing type-I-plus-type-II error.

notation.meaning: Class of transcript laws with bias at least beta.
Bias test based on T oracle calls.

review_flags: exact intended detectability notion is ambiguous between statistical testing, identifiability, and observable bias certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The taxonomy title does not determine whether detectability means uniform hypothesis testing, identifiability, or an observable certificate. The proposed testing definition therefore requires a source specifying the experiment and model classes. In addition, both displayed suprema contain the invalid command sequence `\nautomation` where membership notation was evidently intended; no replacement is returned because the substantive definition remains source-dependent.

children.title: Noise-Tail Classes
children.top_down_role: Variability classes requiring different concentration and robustness mechanisms.

children.title: Bounded Noise
children.top_down_role: Response variability confined to a prescribed bounded range.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure norm bound on the stochastic response error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be an oracle response, let \(m_t=\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\), and define \(\xi_t=G_t-m_t\). The response noise is conditionally bounded with radius \(B<\infty\) when \(\lVert\xi_t\rVert\le B\) almost surely for every \(t\), where the norm is fixed in advance. Equivalently, conditional on every admissible history, the support of \(G_t-m_t\) lies in the closed radius-\(B\) norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise is bounded when its deviation from the conditional mean never exceeds a fixed norm radius.
assumptions_latex: \(G_t\) is conditionally integrable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).
A norm on \(\mathbb R^d\) and a finite radius \(B\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G_t-\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\rVert\le B\) almost surely for every \(t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: almost-sure norm boundedness is the standard bounded-noise class
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The almost-sure bound about the conditional mean is precise and condition fits the leaf, but bounded oracle noise is also commonly defined relative to a target response rather than the conditional mean. An authoritative locator is needed to establish the intended convention for this taxonomy.

children.title: Light-Tailed Noise
children.top_down_role: Response variability governed by rapidly decaying tails.

knowledge_statements.title: Light-Tailed Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional sub-Gaussian control of every one-dimensional projection of response noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_t\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\). It is conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, hence light-tailed, when for every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\langle u,\xi_t\rangle)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2\lVert u\rVert_2^2/2)\) almost surely. Consequently, each projection obeys \(\Pr(\lvert\langle u,\xi_t\rangle\rvert\ge r\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\le2\exp(-r^2/(2\sigma^2\lVert u\rVert_2^2))\) for \(u\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Light-tailed noise has conditionally sub-Gaussian projections, giving Gaussian-type exponential tail decay in every direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) almost surely.
The sub-Gaussian scale \(\sigma<\infty\) is uniform over calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every projection \(\langle u,\xi_t\rangle\) has the stated conditional sub-Gaussian moment and tail bounds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional sub-Gaussian projection control is a standard light-tail oracle assumption
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional vector sub-Gaussian condition and its projection tail bound are mathematically consistent, but “light-tailed” can denote broader sub-exponential or finite-exponential-moment classes. A source is required to confirm that this terminal container is intended specifically for uniform conditional sub-Gaussian noise.

children.title: Heavy-Tailed Noise
children.top_down_role: Response variability permitting substantial tail mass or limited moment control.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tailed Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite low-order moments without an assumed exponential-tail bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in(1,2]\). Centered response noise \(\xi_t\in\mathbb R^d\) belongs to a conditional heavy-tailed \(p\)-moment class with scale \(M\) when \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_t\rVert^p\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le M^p\) almost surely for every \(t\), while no bounded-support, sub-Gaussian, or other exponential-moment condition is imposed. Thus the class permits polynomial tails; conditional Markov's inequality gives \(\Pr(\lVert\xi_t\rVert\ge r\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\le(M/r)^p\) for every \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heavy-tailed noise is controlled only by a finite low-order moment, permitting polynomial tails and excluding any assumed exponential concentration.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) almost surely.
A moment order \(p\in(1,2]\) and finite scale \(M\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_t\rVert^p\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le M^p\) and \(\Pr(\lVert\xi_t\rVert\ge r\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\le(M/r)^p\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite p-moment noise without exponential-tail assumptions is a common heavy-tail model
taxonomy may intend a broader heavy-tail class than the selected p-moment version
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A finite conditional p-moment assumption is a common robust-optimization model, but the stated class also contains bounded and sub-Gaussian distributions because it merely omits, rather than negates, exponential-tail assumptions. A source is needed to confirm whether this leaf denotes that broad moment class or distributions that are genuinely heavy-tailed.

children.title: Sampling Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sampling protocols ranging from fresh independent draws to temporally dependent oracle states.

children.title: Independent Sampling
children.top_down_role: Protocols supplying fresh draws without modeled dependence across interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional factorization of sampling innovations across oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_t\) be the observation used at call \(t\), and let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain all preceding queries, samples, responses, and algorithmic randomness. Sampling is independent from a fixed distribution \(P\) when \(\mathcal L(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P\) almost surely for every \(t\). Consequently, for every horizon \(T\), the joint sample law factors as \(\mathcal L(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T)=P^{\otimes T}\), even though each query \(x_t\) may be chosen adaptively from \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every call, the sample has the same population law and is independent of all previous interaction history; consequently, the samples have the corresponding product law.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_t\) takes values in a common observation space \(\mathcal Z\).
\(P\) is a fixed probability distribution on \(\mathcal Z\).
\(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contains the complete pre-call interaction history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P\) for every \(t\), hence \((Z_1,\ldots,Z_T)\sim P^{\otimes T}\) for every finite horizon \(T\).

notation.meaning: Complete interaction history before call t.

source_refs.source_title: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
source_refs.locator: 2.1 A Formal Model - The Statistical Learning Framework p. 33

review_flags: sequential conditional formulation requires confirmation beyond the i.i.d. learning setup

source_witnesses.source_title: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 A Formal Model - The Statistical Learning Framework p. 33

children.title: Dependent Sampling
children.top_down_role: Protocols carrying temporal, spatial, or transcript-linked dependence across draws.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General temporal dependence among samples used by a stochastic first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an algorithm generate queries \(X_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(\Xi_t\) denote the random sample used to form the oracle response at time \(t\). The oracle has dependent sampling when, conditional on the query sequence, the joint law of \((\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_T)\) need not factor into its one-time conditional marginals. Equivalently, for some \(t\ge 2\), \[\mathcal L(\Xi_t\mid X_{1:T},\Xi_{1:t-1})\ne \mathcal L(\Xi_t\mid X_{1:T}).\] The definition permits arbitrary temporal coupling unless additional mixing, stationarity, or conditional-unbiasedness assumptions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Samples used at different oracle calls are dependent after conditioning on the query sequence; no mixing or stationarity is implied.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge 2\) oracle calls are defined on a common probability space.
Regular conditional distributions exist for the sample variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(\Xi_{1:T}\mid X_{1:T})\ne\prod_{t=1}^{T}\mathcal L(\Xi_t\mid X_{1:T})\) is permitted.

notation.meaning: sample used by the oracle at call t
conditional law of Z given W

review_flags: Terminology varies between dependent-data, correlated-sampling, and Markovian-oracle models.
REQUEST_SOURCES: an authoritative source defining the unrestricted conditional-law formulation is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports this unrestricted conditional-law definition. The LaTeX says nonfactorization is permitted, whereas the plain statement says dependence is present; an authoritative source must also settle whether this leaf denotes actual dependence or merely an oracle class allowing dependence.

children.title: Stateful Sampling
children.top_down_role: Protocols whose response distribution depends on an evolving internal oracle state.

knowledge_statements.title: Stateful Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling generated by an oracle whose persistent internal state evolves between calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stochastic oracle has stateful sampling if there are measurable state and sample spaces, an internal state \(S_t\), and kernels \(K_t\) such that, after receiving query \(X_t\), it jointly generates the sample and next state according to \[(\Xi_t,S_{t+1})\mid(S_t,X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\sim K_t(\,\cdot\mid S_t,X_t).\] The returned response is a measurable function of \((X_t,\Xi_t,S_t)\). The state persists across calls, so marginalizing \(S_t\) can produce dependent samples even when each kernel uses fresh auxiliary randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle carries an internal state across calls; its current sample and next state are generated from that state and the current query.
assumptions_latex: The state, sample, and query spaces are measurable spaces.
\(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contains the transcript before query \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\Xi_t,S_{t+1})\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal F_{t-1}\mid(S_t,X_t)\).

notation.meaning: persistent oracle state before call t

review_flags: The boundary between stateful sampling and general dependent sampling requires a taxonomy-specific source.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source formalizing persistent-state stochastic oracles is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The persistent-state kernel formulation is mathematically coherent and definition is the appropriate content kind, but no source supports this exact oracle model or distinguishes it from the broader dependent-sampling leaf.

children.title: Transcript-Dependent Corruption Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Response corruption classified by dependence on transcripts and by contamination mechanisms.

children.title: Oblivious Noise
children.top_down_role: Response corruption selected independently of the realized interaction transcript.

knowledge_statements.title: Oblivious Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-independent corruption fixed before, or generated independently of, the optimization interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\) be the query, \(G(X_t)\) the ideal response, and \(Y_t=G(X_t)+E_t\) the observed response. The noise is oblivious if the entire noise process \(E_{1:T}\) has a law fixed independently of the algorithm's internal randomness and clean interaction transcript. Thus \[\mathcal L(E_{1:T}\mid X_{1:T},G(X_{1:T}),U)=\mathcal L(E_{1:T}),\] whenever the displayed conditional law is defined. Obliviousness does not require the variables \(E_t\) to be mutually independent, identically distributed, unbiased, or bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The noise process is fixed independently of the algorithm and clean transcript, although its values may remain temporally dependent or biased.
assumptions_latex: The additive corruption model \(Y_t=G(X_t)+E_t\) is used.
\(U\) denotes all algorithmic randomization independent of the oblivious noise process.
review_flags: Oblivious adversary and oblivious stochastic-noise conventions are not universally identical.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source matching the transcript-independent process definition is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted independence from the realized query sequence is generally invalid when later adaptive queries encode earlier noisy responses. A source is required to specify the intended oblivious information pattern and whether independence is ex ante, conditional on a clean counterfactual transcript, or relative to another filtration.

children.title: Adaptive Noise
children.top_down_role: Response corruption permitted to depend on prior queries or responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corruption whose conditional law may react to the optimization transcript available before each response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the queries and responses preceding call \(t\), let \(X_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and write \(Y_t=G(X_t)+E_t\). The noise is adaptive when its conditional distribution may be selected as a measurable kernel of the available transcript and current query: \[E_t\mid(\mathcal F_{t-1},X_t)\sim Q_t(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},X_t).\] Any moment, magnitude, contamination-budget, or nonanticipation restriction on \(Q_t\) is an additional assumption; adaptivity alone supplies none.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each call, the noise distribution may depend on the prior transcript and current query, subject only to separately stated restrictions.
assumptions_latex: The additive response model \(Y_t=G(X_t)+E_t\) is used.
The corruption is nonanticipating: it depends only on information available through the current query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(E_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},X_t)=Q_t(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},X_t)\) may vary with the transcript.
review_flags: Adaptive noise may alternatively mean dependence on past noise but not current queries.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source fixing the intended filtration and adversarial information pattern is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A regular conditional distribution can always be represented by such a kernel, so saying it may depend on the transcript does not by itself distinguish adaptive noise. A source must define the adversary's information and whether actual transcript dependence or merely permission to adapt is intended.

children.title: Contaminated Noise
children.top_down_role: Response corruption arising from replacement, mixture, or outlier-generating mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Contaminated Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional epsilon-contamination of a nominal stochastic oracle response distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each query \(x\), let \(P_x\) be the nominal response law. An oracle has \(\varepsilon\)-contaminated noise if its response at call \(t\), conditional on the available transcript and query \(X_t=x\), has distribution \[\widetilde P_{t,x}=(1-\varepsilon)P_x+\varepsilon Q_{t,x},\qquad 0\le\varepsilon<1,\] where \(Q_{t,x}\) is an arbitrary probability distribution on the response space. Whether \(Q_{t,x}\) may depend on the transcript, and whether contamination indicators are independent across calls, must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each response law is a mixture of the nominal law and an arbitrary contaminating law with probability weight epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(P_x\) and \(Q_{t,x}\) are probability measures on a common measurable response space.
A fixed contamination fraction \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},X_t=x)=(1-\varepsilon)P_x+\varepsilon Q_{t,x}\).

notation.meaning: nominal response distribution at query x

review_flags: The statement uses the Huber mixture-contamination convention; replacement and total-variation conventions differ.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a robust-statistics or robust-oracle source with the exact convention is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record consistently states conditional Huber mixture contamination and uses the correct definition content kind, but no source establishes that this taxonomy uses the mixture convention rather than replacement or total-variation contamination, or specifies transcript dependence across calls.

children.title: Cross-Query Randomness Coupling
children.top_down_role: Protocols coordinating randomness across multiple evaluations or query points.

children.title: Paired Randomness
children.top_down_role: Matched random inputs used across a designated pair of evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired Randomness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A designated pair of oracle calls evaluated under an explicitly coupled pair of random inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x,x'\in\mathbb R^d\) be two queries, and let \(P_x,P_{x'}\) be their prescribed sampling marginals. A paired-randomness oracle draws \((\Xi,\Xi')\) from a specified coupling \(\pi_{x,x'}\) satisfying \[\pi_{x,x'}(A\times\Omega)=P_x(A),\qquad \pi_{x,x'}(\Omega\times B)=P_{x'}(B),\] and returns the paired responses \((H(x,\Xi),H(x',\Xi'))\). The coupling, rather than independence, determines the covariance of the two responses; no coupling across other calls is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two designated queries receive jointly sampled random inputs with prescribed marginals and an explicitly chosen coupling.
assumptions_latex: The two sampling laws are probability measures on a common measurable sample space.
The response map \(H\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\Xi,\Xi')\sim\pi_{x,x'}\in\Pi(P_x,P_{x'})\).

notation.meaning: coupling assigned to the query pair
set of couplings with marginals P_x and P_x'

review_flags: Paired randomness is not a universally standardized oracle term.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source distinguishing pairwise coupling from common-random-number access is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the nonstandard term or its separation from common-randomness coupling. The covariance claim additionally requires integrable square-valued responses; without that hypothesis covariance need not exist.

children.title: Common-Randomness Coupling
children.top_down_role: Shared random sources coordinated across multiple query points or evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Randomness Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple query responses evaluated using the same random input or seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(x,\xi)\) be a stochastic oracle response and let \(P\) be a query-independent law on the sample space. Under common-randomness coupling, a single draw \(\Xi\sim P\) is reused for designated queries \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), producing \[(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)=\bigl(H(x_1,\Xi),\ldots,H(x_m,\Xi)\bigr).\] Each response has its required marginal law, while their joint law is the pushforward of the same \(\Xi\). Reuse applies only to the designated group unless the oracle specification states otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single random draw is reused to evaluate several designated queries, coupling their responses while preserving each marginal response law.
assumptions_latex: The sample law \(P\) is valid for every designated query.
The response map \(H(x,\xi)\) is measurable in \(\xi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_j=H(x_j,\Xi)\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with one shared \(\Xi\sim P\).
review_flags: Common random numbers are standard, but no supplied locator directly supports this oracle-level definition.
REQUEST_SOURCES: an authoritative simulation or stochastic-optimization source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-draw construction is mathematically coherent and fits a definition leaf, but no inspectable citation supports this oracle-level convention or its claimed boundary relative to paired randomness.

children.title: Cross-Query Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence structures induced by coordinated randomness across an interaction transcript.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Query Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual statistical dependence among responses associated with distinct oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For queries \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) and stochastic responses \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T\), cross-query dependence is present when conditioning on the realized queries does not make the responses mutually independent. Thus, for some \(T\ge2\), \[\mathcal L(Y_{1:T}\mid X_{1:T})\ne\prod_{t=1}^{T}\mathcal L(Y_t\mid X_{1:T}).\] This property concerns the joint response law and does not specify its mechanism: shared samples, persistent state, correlated seeds, or adaptive corruption may each induce it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Responses to distinct queries remain statistically dependent after conditioning on the queries; the definition does not prescribe the coupling mechanism.
assumptions_latex: All queries and responses are defined on a common probability space.
Regular conditional response laws given the query sequence exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Y_1,\ldots,Y_T)\) are not conditionally mutually independent given \(X_{1:T}\).
review_flags: Conditioning conventions can differ for adaptive queries because future queries encode past responses.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source specifying the intended conditional-independence convention is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source fixes the conditional-independence convention. For adaptive algorithms, conditioning on the entire realized query sequence can reveal past responses and create or erase apparent dependence, so the intended filtration must be sourced before the formula is reliable.

children.title: Partial-Information Access Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing selected components, coordinates, blocks, samples, or agents rather than complete local information.

children.title: Component-Indexed Access Family
children.top_down_role: Indexed and sampled access to reusable components of a decomposed objective.

children.title: Indexed Component-Value Access
children.top_down_role: Value access to a selected reusable objective component.

knowledge_statements.title: Indexed Component-Value Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-only access to a user-selected component of a finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) have a labeled decomposition \[f(x)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x).\] An indexed component-value oracle accepts a query \((x,i)\) with \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f_i\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and returns \(f_i(x)\). The caller selects the index, and repeated use of the same index addresses the same component. No derivative, subgradient, proximal point, or value of another component is supplied unless separately specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a point and a caller-selected reusable component index, the oracle returns only that component's objective value.
assumptions_latex: The component labeling \(i\mapsto f_i\) is fixed across oracle calls.
The queried point belongs to the selected component's effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{val}}(x,i)=f_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: objective component with persistent label i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard value-oracle specialization for a labeled finite-sum objective.
REQUEST_SOURCES: supplied locators do not directly state indexed component-value access.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, internally consistent, and well matched to the value-access leaf, but it has no citation. The supplied standard-field rationale can support candidate status, not source-backed review of the exact persistent-label and value-only oracle convention.

children.title: Indexed Component First-Order Access
children.top_down_role: First-order access to a selected reusable objective component.

knowledge_statements.title: Indexed Component First-Order Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order access to a user-selected component of a labeled finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x)\), where every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex. An indexed component first-order oracle accepts \((x,i)\) with \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f_i\) and returns \[(f_i(x),g_i),\qquad g_i\in\partial f_i(x).\] If the smooth convention is declared, the second output is \(g_i=\nabla f_i(x)\). The caller controls \(i\), and the same index identifies the same component across calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a caller-selected component index, the oracle returns that component's value and a subgradient, or its gradient under the smooth convention.
assumptions_latex: The component labeling is persistent across oracle calls.
Each selected component is proper and convex, and the query lies in its subdifferentiability domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{1st}}(x,i)=(f_i(x),g_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of component i at x

children.title: Random Component Access
children.top_down_role: Component selection controlled by a prescribed or oracle-mediated sampling law.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Component Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-oracle access whose index is drawn from a specified sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x)\), and let \(p_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x)\) be a prescribed probability distribution on \(\{1,ldots,n\}\). A random component oracle, queried at \(x\), draws \[I_t\sim p_t(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x)\] and returns an allowed component response \(R_{I_t}(x)\), together with \(I_t\) when index disclosure is part of the model. Uniformity, independence across calls, and algorithmic control of the sampling law are separate specifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle samples a component index from a prescribed law and returns the permitted information for that sampled component.
assumptions_latex: The sampling probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one.
The component-response map \(R_i(x)\) is defined for every index with positive sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{rand}}(x)=(I_t,R_{I_t}(x))\) with \(I_t\sim p_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x)\).

notation.meaning: random component index at call t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: randomized incremental methods conventionally sample a component index before obtaining component information.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a direct oracle-model source is needed to settle index disclosure and control of the sampling law.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The index set contains the malformed expression \(\{1,ldots,n\}\), which should use \(\ldots\). More importantly, no source settles whether the index is disclosed or whether the law is prescribed, algorithm-controlled, or oracle-controlled, so the exact definition remains unreliable.

children.title: Batched Component Access Regimes
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous access to selected or sampled subsets of reusable components.

children.title: Selected-Subset Component Access
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous access to a deliberately chosen collection of reusable components.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Subset Component Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batched component access in which the caller explicitly chooses the queried subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x)\), and let \(R_i(x)\) denote the permitted information from component \(i\). A selected-subset component oracle accepts a point \(x\) and a caller-chosen subset \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), then returns \[\mathcal O_B(x)=\bigl(R_i(x)\bigr)_{i\in B}.\] The cost is measured by the declared batch convention, commonly \(|B|\) component evaluations. The subset may depend on the previous transcript; random or oracle-selected batches are different access regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The caller chooses a subset of component indices, and the oracle returns the permitted response for every selected component.
assumptions_latex: Component labels remain fixed across calls.
The response \(R_i(x)\) is defined for each selected index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_B(x)=(R_i(x))_{i\in B}\) for the submitted subset \(B\).

notation.meaning: permitted value or first-order component response

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the definition is the direct batched extension of indexed component access.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a direct source is needed for the batch-cost and transcript-dependent selection conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The caller-selected subset construction fits the definition leaf, but no citation supports the exact access and transcript conventions. The additional claim that cost is commonly \(|B|\) evaluations is model-dependent and also requires a source or explicit removal.

children.title: Sampled-Batch Component Access
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous access to a randomly selected collection of reusable components.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampled-Batch Component Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random mini-batch access to a finite-sum objective at one query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x)\) on \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), with every \(f_i\) differentiable. A sampled-batch component oracle with batch size \(b\) draws a random multiset or subset \(B\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) according to a specified distribution \(P\) and, at query \(x\), returns \(\{(i,f_i(x),\nabla f_i(x)):i\in B\}\), or an explicitly declared subcollection of these fields. The batch-gradient response is \(g_B(x)=b^{-1}\sum_{i\in B}\nabla f_i(x)\), with multiplicities counted. Unbiasedness is an additional property, not part of the access definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle randomly draws a prescribed-size batch of component indices and reveals their values or gradients at the query point; the resulting batch gradient need not be unbiased unless specified.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(f_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
\(1\le b\le n\), with the sampling law \(P\) fixed as part of the oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{P,b}(x)=\{(i,f_i(x),\nabla f_i(x)):i\in B\},\quad B\sim P.\)

notation.meaning: sampled index batch, possibly with multiplicities
declared probability law for the batch
uniform average of sampled component gradients

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the sampled-batch access leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source is supplied for the oracle fields, batch law, multiplicity convention, or optional batch-gradient response.

children.title: Batch Composition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing batch size, replacement, overlap, or component eligibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Composition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal regimes determining how component indices compose a finite batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set \(I=\{1,ldots,n\}\), a size-\(b\) batch is either an ordered tuple \(B\in I^b\), allowing repeated indices, or a subset \(B\subseteq I\) with \(|B|=b\), forbidding repetition. A composition regime specifies the admissible batch family and its law or selection rule. Standard regimes include independent sampling with replacement, sampling without replacement, stratified composition \(B=\bigcup_{h=1}^{H}B_h\) with \(B_h\subseteq I_h\) for a partition \(I=\bigsqcup_{h=1}^{H}I_h\), and deterministic selected-subset composition. Any estimator formed from the batch must state whether repeated indices carry multiplicity and whether component weights are uniform or importance-corrected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch-composition regime fixes whether indices may repeat, how strata contribute, and whether selection is random or deterministic, together with the weighting convention used by batch estimators.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,ldots,n\}\) is finite and \(1\le b\le n\).
For stratification, \(I=\bigsqcup_{h=1}^{H}I_h\) is a declared partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\in I^b\), or \(B\subseteq I\) with \(|B|=b\), according to the declared composition regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed taxonomy of composition regimes or weighting conventions. In addition, every occurrence of the intended index set uses the malformed text \(\{1,ldots,n\}\) rather than \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

children.title: Coordinate-Derivative Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Derivative Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact partial-derivative access for one selected scalar coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be open and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable. A coordinate-derivative oracle accepts a query \((x,j)\in X\times\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and returns the scalar partial derivative \(\partial_j f(x)=\langle\nabla f(x),e_j\rangle\). If value access is explicitly included, the response is \((f(x),\partial_j f(x))\); otherwise the oracle exposes no unqueried derivative coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a point and one coordinate index, the oracle returns that coordinate's partial derivative, optionally together with the objective value, without exposing unqueried derivative coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is open.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at the queried point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{coord}}(x,j)=\partial_j f(x)=\langle\nabla f(x),e_j\rangle.\)

children.title: Coordinate-Friendly Operator Access
children.top_down_role: Partial operator evaluation whose cost reflects coordinate structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Friendly Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-based condition for evaluating selected coordinates of an operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\), let \(P_j\) project onto coordinate block \(V_j\) in a fixed decomposition into \(m\) comparable blocks, and let \(C(T)\) denote the cost of evaluating all of \(T(x)\). The operator access is coordinate-friendly if every requested response \(P_jT(x)\) can be computed without forming all of \(T(x)\) and there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(x\), \(j\), and the decomposition size within the stated computation family, such that \(C_j(T)\le c\,C(T)/m\), apart from explicitly declared decomposition-independent overhead. This condition concerns evaluation cost and does not assert separability, monotonicity, or convergence of a coordinate-update method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator access is coordinate-friendly when any requested output block can be evaluated without forming the full output and, under the declared cost model, costs at most a constant multiple of one block's share of a full evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) has a fixed decomposition into \(m\) comparable output blocks.
\(C(T)\) and \(C_j(T)\) are measured in the same computation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_j(T)\le c\,C(T)/m\quad\text{for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\)

cost of a full operator evaluation

children.title: Extended Block Access
children.top_down_role: Partial access through blocks enlarged beyond a base coordinate partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Block Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local block access enlarged by a declared dependency neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to\mathbb{R}^d\) and let \(B_1,ldots,B_m\) be core coordinate blocks. An extended block-access specification assigns each core block \(B_k\) an evaluation set \(E_k\supseteq B_k\). A query \((x,k)\) may read \(P_{E_k}x\) and returns \(P_{B_k}T(x)\), provided the response is determined by the permitted local state: whenever \(P_{E_k}x=P_{E_k}y\), one has \(P_{B_k}T(x)=P_{B_k}T(y)\). Thus the extension enlarges the coordinates readable for computing a core-block response without granting unrestricted access to the full state or operator output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To compute one core output block, the oracle may inspect a declared larger neighborhood, but the response must depend only on that permitted neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is single-valued.
For every \(k\), the declared evaluation set satisfies \(B_k\subseteq E_k\subseteq\{1,ldots,d\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{E_k}x=P_{E_k}y\Longrightarrow P_{B_k}T(x)=P_{B_k}T(y).\)

notation.meaning: core output block requested by the query
extended coordinate set readable for that query

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Coordinate Block Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block access on an augmented state containing maintained auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the maintained state be \(u=(x,z)\in X\times Z\), where \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) is the primary variable and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q\) stores auxiliary coordinates. For each primary block \(B_k\), fix an auxiliary index set \(A_k\). It may not inspect primary or auxiliary coordinates outside \(B_k\) and \(A_k\), respectively, unless the access specification explicitly enlarges those sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block query may use selected cached or auxiliary state coordinates alongside the primary block and may return updates to those declared auxiliary coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(u=(x,z)\in X\times Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^q\).
Each query block has declared index sets \(B_k\subseteq\{1,ldots,d\}\) and \(A_k\subseteq\{1,ldots,q\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{aux}}(u,k)=R_k(P_{B_k}x,P_{A_k}z).\)

auxiliary coordinates readable by query k

children.title: Local-Dataset Oracles
children.top_down_role: Queries restricted to data held by a selected worker or owner.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Dataset Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order queries restricted to records owned by one selected data holder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let datasets \(D_1,ldots,D_M\) be held by distinct owners, and let owner \(i\)'s empirical objective be \(F_i(x)=|D_i|^{-1}\sum_{\xi\in D_i}\ell(x;\xi)\). A local-dataset oracle accepts an owner index \(i\), a point \(x\), and an admissible local query \(q\), and computes its response using only \(D_i\). For a full local-gradient query it returns \(\nabla F_i(x)\); for a sampled-record query it returns \(\nabla_x\ell(x;\xi)\) with \(\xi\) sampled from a declared law on \(D_i\). It neither reads another owner's records nor directly returns a cross-owner aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A query is routed to one data owner and is answered solely from that owner's records, either as a local aggregate or a sampled-record response.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1,ldots,D_M\) are finite datasets assigned to distinct owners.
\(\ell(\cdot;\xi)\) is differentiable at the queried point for every accessed record \(\xi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{local}}(i,x,\mathrm{grad})=\nabla F_i(x)=|D_i|^{-1}\sum_{\xi\in D_i}\nabla_x\ell(x;\xi).\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits local-dataset access, but no source supports the owner-isolation rule or the combination of full-local-gradient and sampled-record queries. The dataset list also contains malformed \(ldots\) text.

children.title: Agent-Local Objective Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access to private objective or constraint information attached to network agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Agent-Local Objective Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Private first-order access to an objective or constraint owned by one network agent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents \(i\in\{1,ldots,M\}\) own functions \(f_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and, optionally, constraint mappings \(c_i:X\to\mathbb{R}^{r_i}\). An agent-local objective oracle queried with \((i,x)\) returns information derived only from agent \(i\)'s private functions, such as \((f_i(x),\nabla f_i(x))\) and, when requested and defined, \((c_i(x),Jc_i(x))\). It exposes neither another agent's function information nor the global sum \(\sum_{j=1}^{M}f_j(x)\) unless a separate communication or aggregation operation constructs it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected network agent evaluates only its private objective and constraints at the query point; global or other-agent information requires separate communication or aggregation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is the common query domain.
Each queried \(f_i\) and \(c_i\) is differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_i(x)=\bigl(f_i(x),\nabla f_i(x),c_i(x),Jc_i(x)\bigr)\) for the fields requested and defined.

notation.meaning: private objective owned by agent i
private constraint mapping owned by agent i
Jacobian of the local constraint mapping

children.title: Aggregated-Response Oracles
children.top_down_role: Information exposed only through aggregation across data holders or agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated-Response Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Access revealing only a declared aggregate of owner-local responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let owner \(i\) produce a local response \(r_i(x)\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and let \(S\subseteq\{1,ldots,M\}\) be the participating owners. An aggregated-response oracle returns \(A_S((r_i(x))_{i\in S})\) for a declared aggregation map \(A_S\), while individual \(r_i(x)\) remain outside the oracle output. For weighted first-order aggregation, \(A_S((r_i))=\sum_{i\in S}w_i r_i\), where the weights are declared and \(r_i(x)=\nabla f_i(x)\). The oracle model specifies the participating set, weights or nonlinear aggregate, and any randomness; aggregation alone does not imply privacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle exposes a specified function of several owners' local responses, such as a weighted gradient sum, without including the individual responses in its output.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i(x)\in\mathbb{R}^p\) for every participating owner \(i\in S\).
The aggregation map \(A_S\) and participation rule for \(S\) are fixed as part of the oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{agg}}(x,S)=A_S((r_i(x))_{i\in S});\quad \mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{agg}}(x,S)=\sum_{i\in S}w_i\nabla f_i(x)\) in the weighted-gradient case.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract aggregation-map definition fits the leaf, but no source establishes that individual responses are excluded from the oracle output or supports the stated participation and weighting conventions. The owner index set also contains malformed \(ldots\) text.

children.title: Restricted-Disclosure Oracles
children.top_down_role: Responses constrained by privacy, security, or disclosure policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Disclosure Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle responses filtered through an explicit disclosure-admissibility policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(q,D)\in\mathcal{R}\) be the unrestricted response to query \(q\) on private information \(D\). A restricted-disclosure oracle is a channel \(K(\cdot\mid q,D)\) on an output space \(\mathcal{Y}\) whose released value \(Y\) satisfies a declared policy predicate \(\Phi(q,D,K)=\mathrm{true}\). The policy may impose deterministic redaction, an admissible output set, cryptographic visibility, or a probabilistic privacy condition. For example, record-level \((\varepsilon,delta)\)-differential privacy requires \(K(E\mid q,D)\le e^{\varepsilon}K(E\mid q,D')+\delta\) for every measurable \(E\) and every adjacent \(D,D'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unrestricted answer is transformed into a permitted release whose channel must satisfy an explicit disclosure policy, such as redaction, limited visibility, or differential privacy.
assumptions_latex: \(K(\cdot\mid q,D)\) is a probability kernel on measurable output space \(\mathcal{Y}\).
For the privacy example, adjacency of datasets is fixed and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(0\le\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\sim K(\cdot\mid q,D)\quad\text{and}\quad\Phi(q,D,K)=\mathrm{true}.\)

notation.meaning: release channel applied under the disclosure policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source is supplied for the channel formulation or the differential-privacy example. The expression intended as \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differential privacy instead contains the undeclared text-like variable \(delta\), and the broad policy predicate combines redaction, cryptographic visibility, and probabilistic privacy without sourced common semantics.

children.title: Projection Oracles
children.top_down_role: Nearest-point access to a represented feasible set under a declared geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nearest-point oracle in a declared Hilbertian geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(C\subset H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A projection oracle for \(C\) maps each query \(x\in H\) to the unique point \(P_C(x)\in C\) satisfying \[P_C(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\frac12\lVert z-x\rVert^2.\] Equivalently, its response \(p=P_C(x)\) satisfies \(\langle x-p,z-p\rangle\le 0\) for every \(z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a point, the oracle returns the unique feasible point nearest to it in the declared Hilbert-space norm.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C(x)\) is the unique minimizer of \(z\mapsto \tfrac12\lVert z-x\rVert^2\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the feasible set C

children.title: Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Implicit access to a function through a regularized local subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal access for a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). A proximal oracle accepts \(x\in H\) and returns the unique point \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in H}\left\{f(z)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert z-x\rVert^2\right\}.\] Its response \(p\) equivalently satisfies \((x-p)/\lambda\in\partial f(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns the unique minimizer of the function plus a quadratic penalty centered at the query point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) if and only if \((x-p)/\lambda\in\partial f(p)\).

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of f with parameter lambda

children.title: Resolvent Oracles
children.top_down_role: Implicit inversion access to a set-valued or monotone operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact resolvent access to a set-valued monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and let \(\lambda>0\). A resolvent oracle accepts \(x\in H\) and returns the unique point \[J_{\lambda A}(x)=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}(x).\] Thus its response \(p\) is characterized by \(x\in p+\lambda A(p)\), or equivalently \((x-p)/\lambda\in A(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle implicitly inverts identity plus a scaled maximally monotone operator and returns its unique response.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=J_{\lambda A}(x)\) if and only if \((x-p)/\lambda\in A(p)\).

notation.meaning: resolvent of the scaled operator lambda A

children.title: Variable-Metric Implicit Oracles
children.top_down_role: Projection, proximal, or resolvent access parameterized by changing geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Implicit Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit proximal access parameterized by a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(M:H\to H\) be self-adjoint with \(M\succeq mI\) for some \(m>0\). A variable-metric proximal oracle, queried with \((x,M)\), returns \[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{f}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in H}\left\{f(z)+\frac12\langle M(z-x),z-x\rangle\right\}.\] The response \(p\) is unique and satisfies \(M(x-p)\in\partial f(p)\). Indicator functions yield metric projections, while replacing \(\partial f\) by a maximally monotone operator yields metric resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle solves an implicit local subproblem in a query-dependent positive-definite geometry, encompassing metric proximal, projection, and resolvent access.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite-dimensional.
\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(M\) is self-adjoint and satisfies \(M\succeq mI\) for some \(m>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{f}(x)\) is unique and obeys \(M(x-p)\in\partial f(p)\).

notation.meaning: M is uniformly positive definite with lower bound m
proximal mapping in the M-induced metric

children.title: Exact Linear-Minimization Oracles
children.top_down_role: Exact global linear optimization over the represented set.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Linear-Minimization Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global linear optimization over a represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(E^*\) be its dual, and let \(C\subset E\) be nonempty and compact. An exact linear-minimization oracle for \(C\) accepts \(g\in E^*\) and returns some \[s(g)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle.\] Hence \(\langle g,s(g)\rangle=\min_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle\); when the minimizer is not unique, any minimizing point is a valid response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any linear objective, the oracle returns a globally minimizing feasible point, with arbitrary tie-breaking among minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(C\subset E\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle g,s(g)\rangle=\min_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle\).

notation.meaning: oracle response to the linear objective g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact linear-minimization definition is mathematically coherent and fits the container, but it has no evidence record or inspectable source locator.

children.title: Approximate Linear-Minimization Oracles
children.top_down_role: Linear subproblem access with controlled solution quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Linear-Minimization Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively accurate linear minimization over a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subset E\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(\delta\ge 0\). A \(\delta\)-additive approximate linear-minimization oracle accepts \(g\in E^*\) and returns \(s_\delta(g)\in C\) such that \[\langle g,s_\delta(g)\rangle\le \min_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle+\delta.\] The accuracy parameter is measured in objective-value units and may be supplied with each query.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns a feasible point whose linear objective value exceeds the global minimum by at most the declared additive tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(C\subset E\) is nonempty and compact.
\(\delta\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle g,s_\delta(g)\rangle-\min_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle\le\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error convention is precise and locally consistent, but approximate linear-minimization oracles admit multiple conventions. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required for the selected guarantee.

children.title: Weak Linear Oracles
children.top_down_role: Linear access with tolerance-sensitive or multiplicative response strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Linear Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative improvement access relative to a supplied reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subset E\) be nonempty and compact, and fix \(\rho\in(0,1]\). A \(\rho\)-weak linear oracle accepts \((g,x)\in E^*\times C\) and returns \(s\in C\) satisfying \[\langle g,x-s\rangle\ge \rho\max_{z\in C}\langle g,x-z\rangle.\] Thus the returned atom realizes at least a \(\rho\) fraction of the best linear improvement available from the reference point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a feasible reference point, the oracle obtains a fixed fraction of the largest available linear improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(C\subset E\) is nonempty and compact.
\(g\in E^*\) and \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle g,x-s\rangle\ge\rho\max_{z\in C}\langle g,x-z\rangle\).

notation.meaning: feasible reference point supplied with the query

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplicative improvement formula is internally coherent, but the term weak linear oracle is convention-dependent. No source establishes that this reference-point formulation is the intended version.

children.title: Restricted-Atom Oracles
children.top_down_role: Linear access restricted to declared atom classes or locally available atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Atom Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear minimization over a declared query-dependent atom subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\mathcal A\subset E\) be a nonempty compact atom set, and let \(R(q)\subseteq\mathcal A\) be a nonempty compact set of atoms available under state or query descriptor \(q\). A restricted-atom oracle accepts \((g,q)\in E^*\times Q\) and returns \[a(g,q)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in R(q)}\langle g,a\rangle.\] Its guarantee is relative only to \(R(q)\), not necessarily to the full atom set \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle minimizes a linear objective exactly over the atoms currently declared available, without guaranteeing optimality over all atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subset E\) is nonempty and compact.
\(R(q)\subseteq\mathcal A\) is nonempty and compact for every admissible \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle g,a(g,q)\rangle=\min_{a\in R(q)}\langle g,a\rangle\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed query-dependent restriction model lacks an authoritative source, and the space Q used in the query domain is never introduced. Because restricted-atom oracle conventions vary, the intended mathematical interface cannot be confirmed without evidence.

children.title: Operator-Evaluation Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Evaluation Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise access to an operator value or admissible selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real vector spaces and let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty values on its declared query domain \(D\subseteq X\). An operator-evaluation oracle accepts \(x\in D\) and returns some \(y\in F(x)\). If \(F\) is single-valued, the response is necessarily \(y=F(x)\); if \(F\) is set-valued, the oracle's selection rule may be arbitrary unless an additional selection criterion is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a query point, the oracle returns the operator value when single-valued or an admissible member when set-valued.
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) has nonempty values on \(D\subseteq X\).
\(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The response \(y\) satisfies \(y\in F(x)\).

children.title: Primal–Dual First-Order Oracles
children.top_down_role: Coupled first-order access across primal and dual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual First-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled first-order access for a convex-concave saddle function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) and \(L\subseteq Y\) be convex, and let \(\Phi:K\times L\to\mathbb R\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). A primal–dual first-order oracle queried at \((x,y)\) returns \((g_x,g_y)\) with \[g_x\in\partial_x\Phi(x,y),\qquad g_y\in\partial_y[-\Phi(x,\cdot)](y).\] Equivalently, it evaluates a selection of the saddle operator \((x,y)\mapsto(\partial_x\Phi(x,y),\partial_y[-\Phi(x,\cdot)](y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle jointly returns a primal subgradient and a dual-side subgradient of the negated concave component at the same query.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) and \(L\subseteq Y\) are convex.
\(\Phi\) is convex in its first argument and concave in its second.
The displayed partial subdifferentials are nonempty at \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_x\in\partial_x\Phi(x,y)\) and \(g_y\in\partial_y[-\Phi(x,\cdot)](y)\).

notation.meaning: subgradient of the negated dual-side function

children.title: Best-Response Oracles
children.top_down_role: Optimization access against a fixed opposing variable or strategy.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Response Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimization against a fixed opposing saddle variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty compact sets and let \(\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. A primal best-response oracle accepts \(y\in Y\) and returns \[x^{\mathrm{br}}(y)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\Phi(x,y).\] A dual best-response oracle accepts \(x\in X\) and returns \[y^{\mathrm{br}}(x)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y).\] Either oracle may use arbitrary tie-breaking when its best-response set is not a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Holding one player’s variable fixed, the oracle returns an exact optimizing response for the opposing minimization or maximization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty and compact.
\(\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathrm{br}}(y)\) minimizes \(\Phi(\cdot,y)\), while \(y^{\mathrm{br}}(x)\) maximizes \(\Phi(x,\cdot)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Compactness and continuity make both displayed best-response sets nonempty, and the definition fits the container. However, no source supports the selected minimizer-maximizer orientation or terminology.

children.title: Inexact Structured-Subproblem Access
children.top_down_role: Approximate implementations and verification modes for structured oracle responses.

children.title: Subproblem Error Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structured response quality measured under absolute or scale-dependent criteria.

children.title: Absolute Subproblem Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Structured response quality measured against a scale-independent tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Subproblem Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap criterion for an inexact structured-subproblem response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a nonempty feasible set, let \(Q:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(Q^*=\min_{z\in Z}Q(z)\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). A feasible response \(\widehat z\in Z\) has absolute subproblem accuracy \(\varepsilon\) precisely when \[Q(\widehat z)-Q^*\le\varepsilon.\] The tolerance is expressed in the objective-value scale of the current subproblem and does not depend on the magnitude of \(Q^*\), the initial gap, or another reference residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible approximate solution is absolutely accurate when its subproblem objective exceeds the attained optimum by at most the stated tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is nonempty.
\(Q\) attains a finite minimum \(Q^*\) on \(Z\).
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\) and \(\widehat z\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\widehat z)-Q^*\le\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-gap condition is precise, the condition content kind fits the terminal container, and all variables are introduced. It nevertheless lacks the required authoritative source and specific locator for the chosen absolute-accuracy convention.

children.title: Relative Subproblem Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Structured response quality measured relative to a problem-dependent reference scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Subproblem Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative objective-gap criterion for an inexact structured-subproblem oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a context \(z\), let \(Q_z:Y_z\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(Q_z^*:=\inf_{y\in Y_z}Q_z(y)>-\infty\), and let \(\Delta_z\ge 0\) be a prescribed, context-dependent error scale. Given \(\eta\ge 0\), a returned point \(\widehat y\in\operatorname{dom}Q_z\) has relative subproblem accuracy \(\eta\) with respect to \(\Delta_z\) precisely when \[Q_z(\widehat y)-Q_z^*\le \eta\Delta_z.\] If \(\Delta_z=0\), this convention requires exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem response is relatively accurate when its objective gap is at most a prescribed fraction of a nonnegative context-dependent scale.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_z^*>-\infty\)
\(\Delta_z\ge 0\)
\(\eta\ge 0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_z(\widehat y)-Q_z^*\le\eta\Delta_z\)

notation.meaning: structured subproblem objective at outer context z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally precise and fits the leaf, but the normalization by an arbitrary context-dependent scale is a taxonomy-specific relative-accuracy convention. No source is supplied to establish that this is the intended oracle model.

children.title: Accuracy-Scale Selection
children.top_down_role: Choices of reference scale that distinguish absolute from relative quality assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Scale Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible normalization for relative structured-subproblem error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each outer context \(z\), an accuracy scale is a computable quantity \(\Delta_z\ge 0\) chosen before accepting the subproblem response. It is admissible for a relative-gap test if it has the same units as \(Q_z\), depends only on declared context data and permitted oracle information, and satisfies \(\Delta_z=0\) only when exact subproblem optimality is intended. The requested tolerance is then \(\varepsilon_z:=\eta_z\Delta_z\), and acceptance requires \[Q_z(\widehat y)-Q_z^*\le\varepsilon_z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a computable, dimensionally compatible error scale from declared context data, then multiply it by the requested relative tolerance to obtain the absolute acceptance threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_z^*>-\infty\)
\(\eta_z\ge 0\)
\(\Delta_z\ge 0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_z=\eta_z\Delta_z\) and \(Q_z(\widehat y)-Q_z^*\le\varepsilon_z\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the accuracy-scale leaf, but the proposed admissibility requirements, especially the restriction on zero scales, are design choices rather than universal mathematical requirements. An authoritative source for the intended relative-error interface is needed.

children.title: Context-Responsive Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Response fidelity fixed in advance or selected from the outer query context.

children.title: Fixed Subproblem Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Structured response fidelity predetermined independently of the outer interaction context.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Subproblem Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-independent absolute tolerance for repeated structured-subproblem calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider outer iterations \(k\in\mathbb{N}\) with subproblem objectives \(Q_k:Y_k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and finite infima \(Q_k^*\). A fixed-accuracy regime chooses one tolerance \(\bar\varepsilon\ge 0\), independent of \(k\) and the observed outer history. Every accepted response \(\widehat y_k\in\operatorname{dom}Q_k\) must satisfy \[Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\bar\varepsilon.\] Thus the permitted objective error is constant across all calls, although the subproblems themselves may vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-accuracy oracle uses the same absolute objective-gap tolerance for every subproblem call, regardless of iteration or outer history.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k^*>-\infty\) for every \(k\)
\(\bar\varepsilon\ge 0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\bar\varepsilon\) for every accepted call \(k\)

notation.meaning: subproblem objective at outer iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed absolute-gap condition is coherent and correctly distinguished from adaptive accuracy, but no cited source supports this exact classification of an inexact structured-subproblem oracle.

children.title: Adaptive Subproblem Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Structured response fidelity selected using the outer interaction context.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Subproblem Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-dependent tolerances for successive structured-subproblem calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal H_k\) denote the information available before the subproblem response is accepted. An adaptive-accuracy regime selects a nonnegative tolerance \(\varepsilon_k=E_k(\mathcal H_k)\), where \(E_k\) is a declared measurable or deterministic selection rule. For a subproblem objective \(Q_k\) with finite infimum \(Q_k^*\), an accepted response \(\widehat y_k\) must satisfy \[Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\varepsilon_k.\] The rule may tighten or relax accuracy as the outer context changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive regime chooses each nonnegative subproblem tolerance from information already available at that iteration and accepts only responses meeting that tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k^*>-\infty\)
\(\varepsilon_k=E_k(\mathcal H_k)\ge 0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\varepsilon_k\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The history-dependent tolerance condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf. The precise information restriction and selection-rule formulation are oracle-model conventions requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Outer-Context Fidelity Control
children.top_down_role: Information from the outer query used to govern requested subproblem quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Context Fidelity Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling inner subproblem error to an outer method's current fidelity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\ge 0\) be a declared outer-context scale at iteration \(k\), and suppose the outer analysis permits an inner objective error no larger than \(\phi(r_k)\), where \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing and satisfies \(\phi(0)=0\). Fidelity-controlled access chooses \(\varepsilon_k\le\phi(r_k)\) and accepts \(\widehat y_k\) only if \[Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\varepsilon_k.\] Consequently, whenever \(r_k\to0\), continuity of \(\phi\) at zero implies \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner accuracy is controlled by a declared outer scale, so improving outer fidelity forces the permitted subproblem error toward zero.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k^*>-\infty\)
\(0\le\varepsilon_k\le\phi(r_k)\)
\(\phi(0)=0\) and \(\phi\) is continuous at \(0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k\to0\) implies \(Q_k(\widehat y_k)-Q_k^*\le\varepsilon_k\to0\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated implication follows from the declared envelope assumptions and the content kind fits, but the choice of outer scale and the error-envelope coupling are method-dependent. No source identifies this formulation as the intended fidelity-control principle.

children.title: Response Certification Classes
children.top_down_role: Approximate subproblem responses distinguished by availability of verifiable quality evidence.

children.title: Certified Responses
children.top_down_role: Approximate structured responses accompanied by verifiable quality evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable upper bound on a returned subproblem point's objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization subproblem \(Q:Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), a certified response at tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is a pair \((\widehat y,L)\) such that \(\widehat y\in\operatorname{dom}Q\), the supplied data permit independent verification of \(L\le Q^*:=\inf_{y\in Y}Q(y)\), and \[Q(\widehat y)-L\le\varepsilon.\] These two checks imply \(0\le Q(\widehat y)-Q^*\le Q(\widehat y)-L\le\varepsilon\), so the response certifies the requested objective-gap accuracy.

children.title: Certificate-Availability Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Availability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary separating verifiable from merely asserted subproblem accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a response exposes only \(\widehat y\), \(Q(\widehat y)\), and an asserted tolerance \(\varepsilon\), while the caller has no independently valid lower bound on \(Q^*\) and no equivalent residual-to-gap implication. Then the inequality \(Q(\widehat y)-Q^*\le\varepsilon\) is not verifiable from the response alone: two admissible subproblems can agree on all exposed data at \(\widehat y\) yet have optimal values differing by more than \(\varepsilon\). Certification becomes available only after adding information that bounds \(Q^*\) or otherwise controls the gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point value and claimed tolerance cannot certify optimality without additional information bounding the optimum or converting a verifiable residual into an objective-gap bound.

No valid lower bound or residual-to-gap implication is available

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Membership Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Boolean membership queries for explicitly specified points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a fixed set in a space \(X\). A strong membership oracle for \(C\) is a map \(M_C:X\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying \[M_C(x)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in C\] for every explicitly represented query point \(x\in X\). Thus every query receives the exact membership truth value, including points on \(\partial C\); no tolerance band or indeterminate answer is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong membership oracle returns the exact yes-or-no membership status of every explicitly represented query point, including boundary points.

Query points \(x\in X\) have an explicit representation
