knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-adapted certificate sequence with explicitly declared fixed-time validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}\) be a filtration, let \(X_t\) be an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable output, let \(S_t\) be its declared accuracy set, and let \(C_t\in\{0,1\}\) be an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable certificate decision for every \(t\ge1\). The sequence \((C_t)_{t\ge1}\) is a marginally valid sequential certificate at error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if \[\mathbb P\!\left(C_t=1\ \Rightarrow\ X_t\in S_t\right)\ge1-\alpha\qquad\text{for every deterministic }t\ge1.\] These marginal inequalities are time-indexed and do not by themselves assert simultaneous validity or validity at a data-dependent stopping time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginally valid sequential certificate is updated from the transcript and is correct at each declared deterministic time; these fixed-time guarantees alone do not ensure simultaneous or optional-stopping validity.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}\) is the oracle-transcript filtration.
For each \(t\ge1\), \(X_t\) and \(C_t\) are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and \(C_t\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(C_t=1\Rightarrow X_t\in S_t)\ge1-\alpha\) for every deterministic \(t\ge1\), without an implied simultaneous or stopping-time guarantee.

notation.meaning: Boolean certificate decision available at time t
declared accuracy set at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transcript adaptation and marginal fixed-time validity are standard sequential interfaces

children.title: Adaptive-Stopping Validity
children.top_down_role: Certificate validity under data-dependent termination or repeated inspection.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Stopping Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity retained when termination depends on the observed transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}\) be a filtration. For every \(t\ge1\), let \(X_t\) be an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable output, let \(S_t\) be its declared accuracy set, and let \(C_t\in\{0,1\}\) be an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable certificate decision. Suppose that, for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{t=1}^{\infty}\{C_t=1\Rightarrow X_t\in S_t\}\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] Then every almost surely finite \((\mathcal F_t)\)-stopping time \(\tau\) satisfies \[\mathbb P\!\left(C_\tau=1\Rightarrow X_\tau\in S_\tau\right)\ge1-\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneously valid certificate remains valid when evaluated at any almost surely finite stopping time selected from the observed transcript.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb P(\forall t\ge1:\ C_t=1\Rightarrow X_t\in S_t)\ge1-\alpha\).
\(\tau\) is an almost surely finite \((\mathcal F_t)\)-stopping time.
For each \(t\ge1\), \(X_t\) and \(C_t\) are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and \(C_t\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(C_\tau=1\Rightarrow X_\tau\in S_\tau)\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: almost surely finite transcript-adapted stopping time
Boolean certificate decision at time t
declared accuracy set at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: simultaneous validity implies validity at an almost surely finite stopping time

children.title: Observable Stopping Certificate Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between analytical error criteria and quantities recoverable from available responses.

children.title: Transcript-Observable Certificates
children.top_down_role: Quality evidence computable from available oracle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Transcript-Observable Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates computable solely from recorded oracle interactions, internal randomness, and declared known inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_t=(U,X_1,Y_1,\ldots,X_t,Y_t)\) contain the algorithmic random seed \(U\), queried points \(X_s\), and oracle replies \(Y_s\) through time \(t\), and let \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(T_t)\). A time-\(t\) certificate value \(C_t\) is transcript-observable if there exists a measurable map \(c_t\) such that \[C_t=c_t(T_t).\] Equivalently, \(C_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. Its computation may use declared known model constants but not unknown instance quantities absent from \(T_t\). This observability condition does not by itself establish the certificate's correctness or coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is transcript-observable when it can be computed measurably from the random seed, queries, oracle replies, and declared known constants; observability alone does not establish validity.
assumptions_latex: The complete available interaction history is represented by \(T_t\).
Any permitted model constants are declared known inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_t\) is transcript-observable if and only if it is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(T_t)\).

notation.meaning: observable oracle transcript through time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transcript observability is formalized by transcript measurability

children.title: Nonobservable Analysis Metrics
children.top_down_role: Performance measures useful for analysis but unavailable as stopping evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonobservable Analysis Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analytical performance quantities that cannot be recovered from the current oracle transcript uniformly over the admissible instance class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be an admissible instance class, let \(T_t\) be the observed transcript at time \(t\), and let \(M_t^{\theta}=m(\theta,X_t)\) be a real-valued performance metric under instance \(\theta\in\Theta\), such as \(f_\theta(X_t)-\inf_x f_\theta(x)\). The metric is nonobservable from \(T_t\) over \(\Theta\) if there is no single measurable function \(h_t\), independent of \(\theta\), such that \[M_t^{\theta}=h_t(T_t)\qquad\mathbb P_\theta\text{-almost surely for every }\theta\in\Theta.\] A nonobservable metric may be used in analysis, but its value cannot directly be evaluated from the transcript as stopping evidence under the stated oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric is nonobservable over an instance class when no single transcript-based computation recovers it almost surely for every admissible instance; it therefore cannot be evaluated directly as transcript-based stopping evidence.
assumptions_latex: \(T_t\) contains all information exposed by the oracle model through time \(t\).
\(\Theta\) is the declared admissible instance class.
\(M_t^{\theta}\) is a real-valued performance metric for each \(\theta\in\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No measurable function of \(T_t\) alone recovers \(M_t^{\theta}\) almost surely for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).

notation.meaning: analysis performance metric at time t under instance theta

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonobservability is failure of uniform recovery by a transcript-measurable function

children.title: Certificate-Cost Accounting
children.top_down_role: Additional query and computational resources required to verify termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Cost Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates optimization work from resources spent constructing and checking certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a run terminating at time \(\tau\), let \(Q_{\mathrm{opt}}(\tau)\) and \(W_{\mathrm{opt}}(\tau)\) denote oracle queries and computation used to generate iterates, while \(Q_{\mathrm{cert}}(\tau)\) and \(W_{\mathrm{cert}}(\tau)\) denote additional resources used only to construct or verify the stopping certificate. Complete resource accounting is \[Q_{\mathrm{tot}}=Q_{\mathrm{opt}}(\tau)+Q_{\mathrm{cert}}(\tau),\qquad W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_{\mathrm{opt}}(\tau)+W_{\mathrm{cert}}(\tau).\] Shared operations are charged once according to a declared convention, and certificate complexity must identify any stronger auxiliary oracle it invokes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total stopping complexity includes both optimization work and all extra oracle calls or computation required to construct and verify the certificate.
assumptions_latex: Optimization and certificate resources are measured in declared query and computation units.
A fixed convention assigns operations shared by iteration and certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{tot}}=Q_{\mathrm{opt}}+Q_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and \(W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_{\mathrm{opt}}+W_{\mathrm{cert}}\), with auxiliary oracle access disclosed.

notation.meaning: computational work in the declared model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive accounting separates base optimization from certification overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive decomposition is a reasonable representation of certificate overhead and matches the terminal role, provided shared work is assigned once and auxiliary oracle access is disclosed. No inspectable complexity-model source supports the accounting convention.

children.title: Oracle-Model Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Information, representation, precision, protocol, and accounting failures invalidating nominal oracle guarantees or comparisons.

children.title: Information Insufficiency
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by an oracle unable to distinguish materially different admissible instances.

children.title: Transcript Nonidentifiability
children.top_down_role: Multiple admissible instances remain compatible with all observed responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Transcript Nonidentifiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishable admissible instances prevent transcript-only certification of differing target properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_1\) be admissible instances inducing the same distribution for the transcript \(T_t\), but let a target property satisfy \(P(\theta_0)=0\) and \(P(\theta_1)=1\). Every transcript-measurable decision \(D_t=d(T_t)\) then has the same distribution under both instances. Consequently, if \(D_t\in\{0,1\}\), \[\mathbb P_{\theta_0}(D_t\ne0)+\mathbb P_{\theta_1}(D_t\ne1)=1.\] Hence no transcript-only certificate can determine \(P(\theta)\) with error strictly below \(1/2\) uniformly over these two instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two instances produce identically distributed transcripts but have different target properties, no transcript-only rule can reliably distinguish them.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal L_{\theta_0}(T_t)=\mathcal L_{\theta_1}(T_t)\).
\(P(\theta_0)\ne P(\theta_1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every transcript-measurable binary decision has worst-case error at least \(1/2\) on \(\{\theta_0,\theta_1\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: identical observation laws yield a two-point indistinguishability bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identical-transcript-law calculation and resulting two-point worst-case error bound are mathematically correct, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. An information-theoretic or oracle-lower-bound source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Information-Degenerate Responses
children.top_down_role: Local information exposes neither a useful direction nor a global distinction.

children.title: Flat Responses
children.top_down_role: Oracle transcripts lacking useful local variation across nearby queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally flat oracle replies can conceal globally better regions in nonconvex classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix finitely many query points \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\in\mathbb R^d\). Choose a smooth nonnegative bump \(b\) whose compact support avoids these points, and define \(f_0(x)=0\) and \(f_1(x)=-b(x)\). A first-order oracle returning \((f(x),
abla f(x))\) gives \[(f_0(x_t),
abla f_0(x_t))=(f_1(x_t),
abla f_1(x_t))=(0,0)\] for every \(t\le T\), although \(\inf f_0=0\) and \(\inf f_1<0\). Thus a finite flat transcript cannot certify global optimality over a class admitting such hidden perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth negative bump placed away from all queried points preserves flat first-order replies while changing the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many points \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\) are queried.
The admissible nonconvex class contains smooth compactly supported perturbations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Identical flat first-order responses do not identify the global optimum value or certify global optimality.

notation.meaning: smooth bump supported away from queried points
indistinguishable objective functions on the queried points

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hidden smooth bump gives a concrete finite-query resisting pair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a fixed finite set of query points and a function class admitting the stated bump, the counterexample is correct and the counterexample kind fits the leaf. The formulation does not itself establish an adaptive or randomized oracle lower bound, and no source is provided for the stated nonconvex-class boundary.

children.title: Uninformative Responses
children.top_down_role: Responses that fail to expose a useful decision direction or discriminator.

knowledge_statements.title: Uninformative Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-independent oracle responses cannot support reliable certification of an instance-dependent binary property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) index admissible instances, and suppose the oracle response kernel is instance-independent: for every query \(x\), every measurable response set \(B\), and every \(	heta_0,	heta_1\in\Theta\), \[K_{	heta_0}(B\mid x)=K_{	heta_1}(B\mid x).\] Under any adaptive algorithm whose internal randomness has the same law for every instance, the full transcript \(T_t\) has the same distribution for all \(	heta\in\Theta\). e P(	heta_1)\) for two admissible instances, then every transcript-measurable decision \(D_t\in\{0,1\}\) satisfies \[\max\!\left\{\mathbb P_{	heta_0}\!\left(D_t
e P(	heta_0)ight),\mathbb P_{	heta_1}\!\left(D_t

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every query receives the same response distribution under every instance, adaptive interaction reveals no instance information, and no transcript-based binary certificate can have worst-case error below one half on two instances with different target properties.
assumptions_latex: For every query \(x\), the response kernel \(K_\theta(\cdot\mid x)\) is identical for all \(\theta\in\Theta\).
The algorithm's internal randomness has the same law under every instance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every transcript-measurable binary decision has worst-case error at least \(1/2\) on \(\{\theta_0,\theta_1\}\).

notation.meaning: oracle response kernel for instance theta at query x

transcript-measurable binary decision at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an instance-independent observation kernel yields identical transcript laws and a two-point indistinguishability bound

children.title: Local-to-Global Indistinguishability
children.top_down_role: Limits on inferring global instance differences from locally identical information.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Indistinguishability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-query failure when locally identical oracle replies conceal separated global solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a deterministic algorithm making at most \(T\) adaptive queries to an oracle \(O_I\) for an instance \(I\). Suppose two instances \(I_0,I_1\) generate identical transcripts under \(\mathcal A\): recursively, \(O_{I_0}(x_t)=O_{I_1}(x_t)\) for every query \(x_t\) selected from the common preceding transcript. Then \(\mathcal A\) returns the same point \(\widehat x\) on both instances. If their solution sets \(S_0,S_1\) satisfy \(\Delta:=\inf\{\lVert u-v\rVert:u\in S_0,v\in S_1\}>0\), then \[\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,S_i)\geq \frac{\Delta}{2}.\] Thus local agreement at all queried points does not identify the global solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical replies at every adaptive query force the same output on two instances; if their solution sets are separated, that output is substantially wrong for at least one instance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is deterministic and makes at most \(T<\infty\) adaptive queries.
\(S_0\) and \(S_1\) are nonempty.
Oracle replies coincide along the complete query transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,S_i)\geq \Delta/2\).

notation.meaning: Distance between the two solution sets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the terminal container, and the deterministic indistinguishability statement is mathematically coherent. No citation is supplied for the oracle model or lower-bound formulation, so source alignment cannot be verified.

children.title: Limited-Feedback Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Partial observations conceal losses, constraints, or directions required for identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Feedback Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial-feedback access fails when distinct instances induce the same adaptive observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be an instance class, let \(F_I(x)\) denote the full response at query \(x\), and let the accessible feedback be \(Y_I(x)=P_x(F_I(x))\), where \(P_x\) may discard coordinates, losses, constraints, or directions. For a policy \(\pi\), suppose there exist \(I_0,I_1\in\mathcal I\) such that the adaptive feedback transcripts have the same law, \[\mathcal L_{I_0}(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T)=\mathcal L_{I_1}(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T),\] while their solution sets satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(S_0,S_1)=\Delta>0\). Every estimator based only on the transcript then has identical output law on both instances and cannot guarantee distance error strictly below \(\Delta/2\) on both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If partial feedback has the same distribution for two instances with separated solutions, transcript-based methods cannot reliably identify both solutions.
assumptions_latex: Queries are selected measurably from the preceding accessible feedback.
The two solution sets are nonempty and separated by \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No transcript-measurable estimator guarantees \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,S_I)<\Delta/2\) for both \(I=I_0\) and \(I=I_1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record matches limited-feedback ambiguity and is appropriately classified as a failure boundary. A source is needed to fix the intended randomized guarantee—almost-sure, high-probability, or expected error—and to support the partial-feedback model.

children.title: Oracle Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies between declared and realized response properties.

children.title: Systematic Bias
children.top_down_role: Persistent response displacement incompatible with the nominal access model.

knowledge_statements.title: Systematic Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A directional conditional-mean error persists throughout the oracle interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For queries \(x_t\) and returned first-order responses \(Y_t\), write \(Y_t=g(x_t)+E_t\), where \(g(x_t)\) is a valid nominal response and \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\) is the history before query \(t\). The oracle has systematic directional bias on an index set \(T_0\) if there exist a unit vector \(u\) and \(\beta>0\) such that \[\left\langle u,\mathbb E[E_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]\right\rangle\geq\beta\qquad\text{almost surely for every }t\in T_0.\] This violates the nominal conditional-unbiasedness requirement \(\mathbb E[E_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]=0\) and permits cumulative displacement of at least \(\beta |T_0|\) in direction \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Systematic bias occurs when the conditional mean oracle error retains a nonzero component in one direction across the interaction.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) is conditionally integrable given \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
\(u\) is a fixed unit vector and \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t\in T_0}\langle u,\mathbb E[E_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]\rangle\geq\beta |T_0|\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the node, and the displayed cumulative conditional-mean inequality follows from the stated persistent directional bias. No source establishes that this directional version is the intended systematic-bias convention for the taxonomy.

children.title: Uncontrolled Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Approximation error without a usable fidelity relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary approximation errors destroy any usable relation between replies and nominal oracle values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reported response have the form \(Y_t=O_I(x_t)+E_t\). Inexactness is uncontrolled when the access specification imposes neither a known deterministic bound on \(E_t\) nor a known probabilistic, moment, relative-error, or summability condition. If every \(E_t\) in the response space is admissible, then for any two instances \(I_0,I_1\) and any query \(x_t\), choosing \[E_t^{(1)}=O_{I_0}(x_t)-O_{I_1}(x_t)\] makes the response under \(I_1\) equal the exact response under \(I_0\). Consequently, arbitrary inexactness can reproduce any finite exact-oracle transcript and provides no uniform identification guarantee over the instance class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without any error bound or fidelity law, errors can transform one instance’s replies into another’s, eliminating uniform identification guarantees.
assumptions_latex: Additive errors may be chosen arbitrarily in the oracle response space.
The algorithm observes only \(Y_t\), not \(E_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite exact transcript for \(I_0\) can be reproduced under \(I_1\) by admissible errors.

notation.meaning: Nominal oracle response for instance I.
Uncontrolled response error at time t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification and transcript-mimicking construction are coherent under arbitrary additive errors in a common response vector space. A canonical source is required to support that unrestricted error class and the resulting identification claim.

children.title: Nonstationary Oracle Behavior
children.top_down_role: Response laws or represented instances drift during interaction.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonstationary Oracle Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle responses or represented objectives vary with time or interaction history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For query space \(X\) and response space \(Y\), let \(K_t(\cdot\mid x,h)\) be the conditional response law at time \(t\), given query \(x\in X\) and prior history \(h\). The oracle is stationary if there exists a single kernel \(K\) such that \(K_t(\cdot\mid x,h)=K(\cdot\mid x)\) for every admissible \(t,x,h\). It is nonstationary if this equality fails: there exist \(s,t,x\) and admissible histories for which the conditional laws differ. Deterministically, this includes replies \(O_t(x)\) representing changing functions \(f_t\), constraints \(C_t\), or operators \(A_t\), rather than one fixed optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle is nonstationary when its response law or represented optimization instance changes with time or interaction history.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_t(\cdot\mid x,h)\) is a probability kernel on the response space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonstationarity means \(K_t(\cdot\mid x,h)\neq K(\cdot\mid x)\) for every candidate fixed kernel \(K\) at some admissible argument.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the node's role and explicitly treats both time variation and history dependence. Because stationarity conventions differ across stochastic-oracle models, an authoritative source is required for the selected history-independent kernel formulation.

children.title: Adversarial Response Corruption
children.top_down_role: Responses are strategically corrupted in dependence on the query history.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Response Corruption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-adaptive corruptions can strategically alter otherwise valid oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\) be selected from history \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\), and let the reported response be \(Y_t=O_I(x_t)+C_t\), where an adversary chooses \(C_t=C_t(\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t,I)\) after observing the available history and current query. This is adversarial response corruption. Under a budget \(\sum_{t=1}^T\lVert C_t\rVert\leq B\), robustness claims must explicitly depend on \(B\) or a stronger corruption constraint. Without any budget, choosing \(C_t=O_J(x_t)-O_I(x_t)\) makes the corrupted transcript of instance \(I\) identical to the exact transcript of any comparison instance \(J\), so uniform identification is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-aware adversary alters each reply strategically; without a corruption budget, it can exactly imitate any comparison instance.
assumptions_latex: The adversary observes the available history and current query before selecting \(C_t\).
Corruptions lie in the oracle response vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With unbounded corruption, \(Y_t=O_J(x_t)\) can be enforced for every \(t\) and any comparison instance \(J\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, and unbounded additive corruption can reproduce a comparison oracle when responses share a vector space. No source is supplied for the history-adaptive corruption model, budget convention, or impossibility interpretation.

children.title: Geometric Representation Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of geometric reductions caused by degenerate, unbounded, or poorly conditioned set representations.

children.title: Geometric Scale-Data Failures
children.top_down_role: Geometric access lacks scale information required for efficient reduction.

children.title: Missing Boundedness Data
children.top_down_role: Access models lacking usable outer-scale or extent information.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Boundedness Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unknown feasible-region or solution-distance scale prevents instantiation of radius-dependent guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be feasible, let \(x_0\in C\), and let \(X^*\neq\varnothing\) be the solution set. Boundedness data consist of a known finite number \(R\) satisfying either \(C\subseteq B(x_0,R)\) or \(\operatorname{dist}(x_0,X^*)\leq R\), according to the algorithmic guarantee. Such data are missing when no certified finite \(R\) is supplied or derivable from the available oracle. A rate or stopping rule containing \(R\), for example \(f(\widehat x_T)-f^*\leq LR/\sqrt T\), then cannot be converted into a certified numerical accuracy or query budget from the available information alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no certified radius bounds the feasible region or initial solution distance, radius-dependent rates and stopping budgets cannot be evaluated.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(X^*\) are nonempty.
The stated method or bound requires a finite radius parameter \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A guarantee depending on unknown \(R\) yields no computable certified choice of \(T\) from the supplied access data alone.

notation.meaning: Required feasible-set or solution-distance radius bound.
Closed Euclidean ball centered at the initial point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly targets the failure caused by unavailable radius data, and the content kind fits. The illustrative rate and the claim about certified query budgets require a specific complexity theorem or textbook locator.

children.title: Missing Rounding Data
children.top_down_role: Access models lacking geometric conditioning or inner-scale information.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Rounding Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absent inner–outer geometric certificates leave conditioning parameters unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty convex set with affine hull \(L=\operatorname{aff}(C)\). Euclidean rounding data are a point \(z\in L\) and certified radii \(0<r\leq R<\infty\) such that \[B_L(z,r)\subseteq C\subseteq B_L(z,R),\qquad B_L(z,\rho):=\{x\in L:\lVert x-z\rVert\leq\rho\}.\] More generally, an invertible affine transformation may provide the corresponding ball sandwich. Rounding data are missing when no such certificate or transformation is supplied or recoverable. Algorithms whose bounds use the aspect ratio \(\kappa=R/r\) then lack an evaluable conditioning parameter, even when membership or separation access to \(C\) is otherwise available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a certified inner and outer ball, the set’s aspect ratio is unknown, so geometry-dependent guarantees cannot be numerically instantiated.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and convex in its affine hull.
The relevant method requires certified inner and outer radii.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounding condition \(\kappa=R/r\) is unavailable from the stated access data.

notation.meaning: Radius-rho ball relative to affine hull L.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals
source_refs.locator: III. Convex Sets p. 87

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals
source_witnesses.locator: III. Convex Sets p. 87

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ball-sandwich formulation is mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits. The cited broad convex-sets locator does not specifically support the rounding certificate, affine transformation formulation, or algorithmic dependence on the aspect ratio.

children.title: Scale-Free Reduction Failures
children.top_down_role: Efficiency losses when reductions proceed without adequate geometric scale controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Free Reduction Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization fails when required geometric scales cannot be inferred from the access model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the ellipsoids \(C_M=A_MB_2^n\), where \(A_M=\operatorname{diag}(M,1,\ldots,1)\) and \(M\geq1\). Their Euclidean inner and outer radii are \(1\) and \(M\), so their aspect ratios are \(M\). A purported scale-free reduction that uses one fixed Euclidean normalization, but receives neither \(M\) nor an affine rounding map, cannot certify a uniform normalized aspect ratio over this family. Therefore any downstream guarantee whose constants require bounded Euclidean diameter, an inscribed radius, or a rounding ratio remains uninstantiated. Affine covariance of the oracle alone does not supply the missing numerical transformation or its conditioning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anisotropically scaled ellipsoids have unbounded aspect ratios; without scale or rounding data, a fixed normalization cannot certify uniformly controlled geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(n\geq2\) and \(B_2^n\) is the Euclidean unit ball.
No value of \(M\) or certified affine rounding map is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No fixed Euclidean normalization certifies a uniformly bounded aspect ratio for \(\{C_M:M\geq1\}\).

notation.meaning: Aspect ratio of the ellipsoid family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ellipsoid example has inner radius 1, outer radius M, and unbounded Euclidean aspect ratio, matching the terminal failure theme. The purported reduction and its available oracle information are not formally specified or sourced, so the broader impossibility claim cannot be reliably assessed.

children.title: Degenerate-Dimension Geometry
children.top_down_role: Full-dimensional weak-oracle interpretations fail on degenerate feasible bodies.

children.title: Lower-Dimensional Sets
children.top_down_role: Feasible bodies contained in a proper affine subspace of the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sets whose affine hull has dimension below that of the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its affine dimension is \(\dim C:=\dim(\operatorname{aff}(C)-x_0)\), where \(x_0\in C\); this value is independent of the selected \(x_0\). The set is lower-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^n\) when \[\dim C<n.\] Equivalently, \(C\) is contained in a proper affine subspace of \(\mathbb R^n\). Geometry and oracle guarantees formulated intrinsically should therefore use \(L=\operatorname{aff}(C)\), its induced norm and topology, and dimension \(\dim L\), rather than assuming that \(C\) is full-dimensional in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is lower-dimensional when its affine hull is a proper affine subspace of the ambient space.
assumptions_latex: \(C\neq\varnothing\) and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is lower-dimensional exactly when \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}(C))<n\).

notation.meaning: Dimension of the affine hull of C.
Affine hull used as the intrinsic ambient space.

children.title: Empty-Interior Sets
children.top_down_role: Feasible bodies lacking ambient interior required by full-dimensional access interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Interior Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient interior may vanish although relative interior remains meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty. If \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\neq\mathbb R^n\), then the ambient Euclidean interior satisfies \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}(C)=\varnothing\), because no ambient open ball can lie in a proper affine subspace. If, additionally, \(C\) is convex, then its relative interior is \[\operatorname{ri}(C):=\{x\in C:\exists\varepsilon>0,\ B(x,\varepsilon)\cap\operatorname{aff}(C)\subseteq C\},\] and \(\operatorname{ri}(C)\neq\varnothing\). Hence an oracle model requiring ambient interior points excludes every lower-dimensional convex feasible set, whereas a relative-interior formulation does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every lower-dimensional set has empty ambient interior, while every nonempty convex set has nonempty interior relative to its affine hull.
assumptions_latex: \(C\neq\varnothing\) and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
For nonemptiness of relative interior, \(C\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\dim C<n\), then \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}(C)=\varnothing\); if \(C\) is convex, then \(\operatorname{ri}(C)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Interior in the ambient Euclidean topology.
Interior relative to the affine hull of C.

children.title: Relative-Interior Access
children.top_down_role: Oracle interpretations adapted to the affine geometry of degenerate feasible bodies.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle queries and neighborhood requirements are interpreted inside the feasible affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, with \(L=\operatorname{aff}(C)\). An oracle model provides relative-interior access if it supplies an initial point \(x_0\in\operatorname{ri}(C)\), permits every required query in \(\operatorname{ri}(C)\), and interprets local neighborhoods relative to \(L\): for each such query \(x\), there exists \(\varepsilon_x>0\) with \[B(x,\varepsilon_x)\cap L\subseteq C.\] If computations require intrinsic coordinates or relative balls, the model must additionally provide a representation of \(L\) sufficient to construct them. This condition remains meaningful when \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}(C)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative-interior access supplies feasible query points and neighborhoods within the set’s affine hull, including when ambient interior is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of \(\mathbb R^n\).
The algorithm's local queries are intended to remain feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All required local neighborhoods are taken in \(L=\operatorname{aff}(C)\), not in the ambient space \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Affine hull of the feasible set.
Relative interior of C in L.
Certified local relative-interior radius at query x.

The cited convex-analysis section supports relative interior but not the stronger oracle requirements concerning supplied initial points, permitted queries, certified radii, or a computational representation of the affine hull.

children.title: Recession-Dominated Geometry
children.top_down_role: Optimization and separation interpretations require additional recession or bounding information.

children.title: Unbounded Sets
children.top_down_role: Feasible regions without finite outer extent under the stated representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-space definition, specialized to feasible sets in finite-dimensional optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty subset of a normed space \((X,\|\cdot\|)\). The set \(C\) is unbounded if
\[
\forall R>0\;\exists x\in C:\ \|x\|>R.
\]
Equivalently, there is no \(R<\infty\) such that \(C\subseteq\{x\in X:\|x\|\le R\}\). In finite dimensions, this is equivalent to the existence of a sequence \((x_k)_{k\ge1}\subseteq C\) satisfying \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty feasible set is unbounded when it contains points of arbitrarily large norm; equivalently, it admits a sequence whose norms diverge.
assumptions_latex: \(C\neq\varnothing\)
\((X,\|\cdot\|)\) is a normed space
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is unbounded}\iff (\forall R>0)(\exists x\in C)\,\|x\|>R\).

children.title: Recession-Dominated Sets
children.top_down_role: Instances whose optimization behavior is governed primarily by recession geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Dominated Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local definition for unbounded closed convex sets completely generated by bounded geometry and recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, with recession cone
\[
C^\infty:=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\ x+td\in C\ \text{for every }x\in C\text{ and }t\ge0\}.
\]
Call \(C\) recession-dominated if there exists a nonempty bounded set \(B\subseteq C\) such that
\[
C=B+C^\infty.
\]
Thus every point of \(C\) is a bounded base point plus a recession direction, and every unbounded sequence in \(C\) can escape only through directions represented by \(C^\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set is recession-dominated when it equals a bounded base plus its recession cone, so all escape geometry is encoded by recession directions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is recession-dominated}\iff(\exists B\subseteq C)(B\neq\varnothing,\ B\text{ bounded},\ C=B+C^\infty)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed bounded-base-plus-recession-cone definition is coherent and fits the leaf, but “recession-dominated” is nonstandard local terminology and no source establishes that this is the intended exact meaning or supports the accompanying escape-geometry assertion.

children.title: Missing Recession Information
children.top_down_role: Access models lacking directional information needed to interpret unbounded behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Recession Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of bounded local oracle transcripts to determine an unbounded feasible set’s recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a deterministic algorithm make finitely many membership or separation queries, all lying in a bounded set \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\). If two nonempty closed convex sets \(C_0,C_1\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(C_0\cap Q=C_1\cap Q\) and admit identical valid oracle responses at every queried point, yet \(C_0^\infty\ne C_1^\infty\), then the transcript does not identify the recession cone. Consequently, no output depending only on that transcript can be guaranteed to recover \(C^\infty\), certify boundedness, or validate conclusions requiring the missing recession directions for both instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded finite transcript cannot determine recession geometry when two compatible convex sets agree locally but have different recession cones.
assumptions_latex: \(C_0,C_1\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty, closed, and convex
The finite query set is contained in a bounded set \(Q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_0^\infty\ne C_1^\infty\Rightarrow\text{the common transcript cannot identify the recession cone uniformly}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A precise indistinguishability result requires a sourced membership/separation-oracle model. Moreover, different recession cones alone do not imply that the two instances differ in boundedness, so the claimed impossibility of certifying boundedness needs the additional hypothesis that one recession cone is trivial and the other is not, or must be removed.

children.title: Boundary Precision Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Finite precision prevents reliable distinction between membership and near-membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Precision Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-distance uncertainty for membership decisions near the boundary of a closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let an approximate membership oracle have tolerance \(\delta>0\): it must answer inside when \(x\in C\), must answer outside when \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)>\delta\), and may return either answer when \(0<\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\delta\). Hence queries in the uncertainty band
\[
U_\delta(C):=\{x:\ 0<\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\delta\}
\]
cannot reliably distinguish membership from near-membership. Exact boundary recovery or exact feasibility certification is therefore unavailable from this oracle without a positive margin or an exact-arithmetic convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With distance tolerance δ, points just outside a closed set may be indistinguishable from feasible points, preventing exact boundary or feasibility decisions without margin assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed
\(\delta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in U_\delta(C)\Rightarrow\text{membership is not determined by the oracle specification}.\)

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to C

children.title: Interaction Integrity Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Invalid independence, reuse, adaptivity, or concurrency interpretations.

children.title: Sampling-Reuse Protocol Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Repeated access to fixed data is analyzed as if responses were fresh samples.

children.title: Fresh-Sample Protocols
children.top_down_role: Access regimes supplying newly sampled information across repeated queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Fresh-Sample Protocols
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional independence and unbiasedness condition for stochastic first-order oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) be the transcript sigma-field before query \(x_t\), with \(x_t\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\). A stochastic first-order oracle follows a fresh-sample protocol if it draws \(\xi_t\) independently of \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and returns \(G_t=G(x_t,\xi_t)\) satisfying
\[
\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial f(x_t),
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|G_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]<\infty.
\]
For differentiable \(f\), the inclusion is replaced by equality with \(\nabla f(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each oracle call uses a sample independent of the prior transcript, making the returned stochastic gradient conditionally unbiased at the adaptive query.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable
\(f\) is proper and convex on \(\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi_t\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial f(x_t)\).

children.title: Fixed-Data Reuse
children.top_down_role: Access regimes repeatedly consulting the same underlying data realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Data Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical-oracle protocol in which every adaptive query is evaluated on one fixed dataset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)\) be sampled once, and define the empirical objective
\[
F_S(x):=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\ell(x;Z_i).
\]
A fixed-data-reuse protocol returns at every round \(t\) a response \(G_t\in\partial F_S(x_t)\), where \(x_t\) may depend on the preceding transcript and hence on \(S\). The dataset is not resampled between calls. Conditional on \(S\), the oracle may be deterministic, but repeated responses are generally not independent under the population-data probability law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One dataset is sampled once and reused for all adaptive queries; responses target the empirical objective and need not be independent across rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(S=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)\) is drawn once
\(x_t\) may depend on earlier responses
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_t\in\partial F_S(x_t)\) for every \(t\), with the same dataset \(S\) used throughout.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-dataset protocol is plausible and appropriately classified as a condition, but it has no source. The subgradient response also implicitly requires suitable convexity and domain assumptions on the empirical objective at every queried point; those assumptions are not introduced.

children.title: Reuse-Induced Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence effects that invalidate fresh-sample interpretations of reused responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Induced Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-bias mechanism caused by repeatedly querying a stochastic oracle built from fixed data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under fixed-data reuse, let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}=\sigma(G_1,\ldots,G_{t-1})\) and let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. Because both \(x_t\) and \(G_t=G_S(x_t)\) depend on the same dataset \(S\), population unbiasedness at each fixed nonrandom point,
\[
\mathbb E_S[G_S(x)]=g(x),
\]
does not imply adaptive conditional unbiasedness
\[
\mathbb E_S[G_S(x_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=g(x_t).
\]
Thus martingale-difference arguments requiring fresh conditional means cannot be transferred to the reuse protocol without an additional stability, independence, or bias bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing one dataset couples adaptive queries and responses, so pointwise population unbiasedness does not guarantee conditional unbiasedness along the realized transcript.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the preceding transcript
\(G_S\) uses the same random dataset at every round
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_S[G_S(x)]=g(x)\ \forall x\) does not generally imply \(\mathbb E_S[G_S(x_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=g(x_t)\).

notation.meaning: oracle constructed from fixed data S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The non-implication from pointwise marginal unbiasedness to adaptive conditional unbiasedness is correct in general and fits the leaf, but it is a substantive statistical claim with no citation. An authoritative adaptive-data or stochastic-approximation source, ideally with a theorem or counterexample locator, is required.

children.title: Adaptive Data Leakage
children.top_down_role: Transcript-dependent reuse compromises nominal statistical validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Data Leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Statistical failure boundary for transcript-adaptive reuse of one evaluation dataset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a fixed sample and let an algorithm choose each query \(q_t:\mathcal Z\to[0,1]\) measurably from earlier empirical answers \(a_s=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m q_s(Z_i)\). For an adaptively selected index \(T\), ordinary fixed-query concentration does not by itself imply
\[
\left|a_T-\mathbb E[q_T(Z)]\right|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The implication fails because \(q_T\) is correlated with \(S\) through the transcript. A valid guarantee therefore requires an explicit adaptive-validity device, such as fresh holdout data, stability, privacy, or a uniform complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choosing evaluations from prior answers can leak information about fixed data, invalidating fixed-query concentration unless an adaptive-validity mechanism is supplied.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are sampled once
Queries are selected adaptively from previous empirical answers
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{fixed-query concentration}\not\Rightarrow |a_T-\mathbb E[q_T(Z)]|\le\varepsilon\) for transcript-adaptive \(T\).

notation.meaning: empirical answer on the reused sample

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon is standard and the content kind fits, but the displayed concentration statement leaves the probability level, sample-size dependence, and quantification over epsilon unspecified. A source is needed to select a precise valid formulation and support the listed adaptive-validity mechanisms.

children.title: Response-Coherence Failures
children.top_down_role: Concurrent responses refer to incompatible instance or state versions.

children.title: Stale Responses
children.top_down_role: Responses reflecting an instance or state older than the active query context.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay model for first-order responses evaluated at an earlier iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates \((x_t)_{t\ge0}\), a first-order response at round \(t\) is stale with delay \(\tau_t\in\{0,\ldots,t\}\) if
\[
G_t\in\partial f(x_{t-\tau_t})
\]
rather than \(G_t\in\partial f(x_t)\). In a bounded-staleness model there is an integer \(\tau_{\max}<\infty\) satisfying \(0\le\tau_t\le\tau_{\max}\) for every \(t\). Any convergence claim based on current-point oracle responses requires a separate argument controlling the discrepancy between \(x_t\) and \(x_{t-\tau_t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale response is computed at an earlier iterate; bounded staleness imposes a uniform maximum delay and requires explicit control of iterate drift.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex
\(0\le\tau_t\le t\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_t\in\partial f(x_{t-\tau_t})\), with bounded staleness when \(\sup_t\tau_t\le\tau_{\max}<\infty\).

children.title: Inconsistent Responses
children.top_down_role: Responses that cannot be interpreted against one coherent instance state.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite transcript criterion for incompatibility with any single convex first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite first-order transcript \(\{(x_i,f_i,g_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) is inconsistent with a convex function oracle if no proper convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfies \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for every \(i\). Equivalently, inconsistency occurs exactly when at least one pair violates the subgradient interpolation inequalities
\[
f_j\ge f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle
\qquad\text{for all }i,j.
\]
Such a transcript cannot represent responses from one fixed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex oracle responses are inconsistent when their reported values and subgradients violate a subgradient inequality, so no single convex objective can generate the transcript.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(f_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{transcript inconsistent}\iff(\exists i,j)\ f_j<f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle.\)

notation.meaning: query, reported value, and reported subgradient

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite convex interpolation equivalence is mathematically correct for the stated finite-valued data, but it is a substantive necessary-and-sufficient result. The cited generic convex-sets locator does not specifically support the subgradient interpolation criterion, so an exact theorem, proposition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Version-Coherence Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incompatible state versions across concurrent oracle interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Version-Coherence Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript failure caused by mixing responses from different objective or dataset versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_t\) identify the objective version used at round \(t\), and suppose the oracle returns \(G_t\in\partial f_{v_t}(x_t)\). A version-coherence failure occurs when an analysis assumes a single fixed function \(f\) but the transcript contains indices \(s,t\) with \(v_s\ne v_t\), without declaring the changes or bounding
\[
\sup_x|f_{v_s}(x)-f_{v_t}(x)|
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sup_x\operatorname{dist}(\partial f_{v_s}(x),\partial f_{v_t}(x)).
\]
Then the transcript need not satisfy the consistency relations of any one objective, and fixed-objective guarantees do not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing undeclared responses from different objective versions can destroy single-objective consistency; fixed-objective guarantees require version identity or explicit drift bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each response is valid for its labeled version \(f_{v_t}\)
The analysis presumes one fixed objective
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\exists s,t)\ v_s\ne v_t\) without version-drift control invalidates the fixed-objective oracle premise.

notation.meaning: objective version used at round t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Different version labels do not by themselves invalidate a fixed-objective premise: the functions may coincide, or the mixed observations may still be compatible with one objective. In addition, the global difference of extended-real-valued functions may be undefined, and the displayed distance between subdifferential sets is not specified and may involve empty sets. A sourced, specialized drift or incompatibility model is required.

children.title: Algorithm–Oracle Randomness Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Guarantees rely on independence or measurability conditions absent from the realized protocol.

knowledge_statements.title: Algorithm–Oracle Randomness Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of conditional-unbiasedness arguments when oracle randomness is coupled to the adaptive algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the algorithm’s past random choices and oracle responses, and let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. A proof requiring a martingale-difference oracle error \(\varepsilon_t:=G_t-g(x_t)\) assumes
\[
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0.
\]
If the oracle seed at round \(t\) is reused, revealed in advance, or otherwise coupled with \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), marginal unbiasedness \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t]=0\) does not ensure this conditional equality. Consequently, guarantees relying on martingale concentration or conditional variance recursions are unsupported unless the realized coupling is modeled and controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginally unbiased oracle noise is insufficient when its randomness is coupled with the adaptive algorithm; martingale-based guarantees require conditional unbiasedness relative to the transcript.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable
The analysis uses conditional-unbiasedness or martingale concentration
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t]=0\not\Rightarrow\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\); without the latter, the stated martingale guarantee is inapplicable.

notation.meaning: joint algorithm-oracle history before round t

children.title: Hidden-Cost Failures
children.top_down_role: Nominal oracle counts cease to predict computational effort.

children.title: Nonuniform Query Cost
children.top_down_role: The cost of a call varies materially with the query, response, or requested fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Query Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unit-cost oracle counting when individual calls have query-dependent implementation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an oracle call with query-response pair \((q,r)\) and requested tolerance \(\eta>0\) have implementation cost \(c(q,r,\eta)\ge 0\). For an algorithm producing transcript \(\tau=((q_t,r_t,\eta_t))_{t=1}^{N}\), its oracle work is \(W(\tau)=\sum_{t=1}^{N}c(q_t,r_t,\eta_t)\). A bound on the query count \(N\) alone does not imply a uniform work bound unless \(c(q,r,\eta)\le \bar c\) over every admissible call, or another explicit bound controls the displayed sum. Thus equal query counts need not represent comparable computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting every oracle call as one unit is invalid when call costs vary and no uniform per-call or aggregate cost bound is supplied.
assumptions_latex: \(c(q,r,\eta)\) measures the chosen computational resource for one admissible call.
The oracle algorithm may choose queries and tolerances adaptively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A query-count bound alone does not control \(W(\tau)\) without a uniform or aggregate cost bound.

children.title: Intractable Structured Oracles
children.top_down_role: A nominal structured oracle hides a computationally hard subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Intractable Structured Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating formal oracle availability from efficient implementability of the oracle response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) encode an optimization instance and let a structured oracle return \(O_I(q)\), where computing \(O_I(q)\) requires solving an auxiliary problem \(S(I,q)\). If some polynomial-time reduction maps every instance \(z\) of a computationally hard problem to \((I_z,q_z)\) such that \(O_{I_z}(q_z)\) determines the answer for \(z\), then an exact unit-cost call to \(O\) hides that hard computation. Consequently, polynomial oracle-query complexity does not establish polynomial runtime unless the oracle is implementable within the asserted resource bound or approximation access is separately analyzed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small number of structured-oracle calls gives no efficient algorithm when producing one exact response solves a computationally hard auxiliary problem.
assumptions_latex: The exact oracle response determines the solution of the reduced hard instance.
Runtime includes the work required to implement oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial query complexity need not imply polynomial runtime.

notation.meaning: Structured-oracle response for instance I and query q.
Auxiliary problem used to implement the response.

children.title: Precision-Cost Explosion
children.top_down_role: Per-query work grows sharply as response accuracy increases.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Cost Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of precision-independent oracle accounting for increasingly accurate approximate responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a query set, let \((Y,d)\) be a metric space, and let \(O:Q\to Y\) be an exact oracle. Suppose an approximate call at tolerance \(\eta>0\) returns \(r_\eta(q)\in Y\) satisfying \(d(r_\eta(q),O(q))\le \eta\). Let \(C(q,\eta)\) be the implementation cost of that call, and suppose \(C(q,\eta)\ge c(\eta)\ge0\) for every admissible \(q\in Q\). If \(c(\eta)\to\infty\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\), then any execution using tolerances \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N\) has oracle work \(W\ge\sum_{t=1}^{N}c(\eta_t)\). Hence an iteration or query bound independent of \(c\) does not imply a runtime bound, particularly when attaining target error \(\varepsilon>0\) forces at least one requested tolerance to approach zero with \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every sufficiently accurate oracle response has a growing implementation-cost lower bound, query complexity that omits the tolerance-cost law can severely understate total work.
assumptions_latex: \(C(q,\eta)\) counts the selected implementation resource for an admissible approximate response.
The accuracy analysis may require requested tolerances to depend on the target error \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle work satisfies \(W\ge\sum_{t=1}^{N}c(\eta_t)\), so the query count \(N\) alone does not control runtime.

notation.meaning: Implementation cost of the approximate response to query q at tolerance eta.
Uniform lower bound on the cost of an admissible response at tolerance eta.
Total oracle implementation work of the execution.

children.title: Communication-Transfer Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Synchronization or data transfer dominates nominal local query cost.

children.title: Communication Dominance
children.top_down_role: Regimes where inter-worker communication outweighs nominal local oracle cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion identifying regimes where message transmission, rather than local arithmetic, determines execution cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a distributed oracle algorithm on instances indexed by size \(n\), decompose execution time as \(T(n)=T_{\mathrm{comp}}(n)+T_{\mathrm{comm}}(n)+T_{\mathrm{sync}}(n)\), using a fixed accounting convention. Communication dominance holds along an instance family when \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(n)/T(n)\to1\) as \(n\to\infty\). More generally, communication is asymptotically dominant over computation when \(T_{\mathrm{comp}}(n)=o(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(n))\). In either case, an oracle-query or flop bound that omits message count, message volume, latency, and topology does not by itself characterize execution time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication dominates when its time asymptotically accounts for nearly all execution time, making query or flop counts alone inadequate.
assumptions_latex: All time components use the same execution model and instance family.
Communication time includes the model's latency and bandwidth costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Query and arithmetic counts alone do not characterize \(T(n)\) under communication dominance.

notation.meaning: Total execution time under the stated accounting convention.

children.title: Data-Movement Dominance
children.top_down_role: Regimes where memory, storage, or network transfer controls total execution cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Movement Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for memory traffic becoming the leading cost of oracle evaluation or iterative updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an implementation indexed by instance size \(n\), let \(B(n)\) be bytes transferred between relevant memory levels and let \(F(n)\) be arithmetic operations. Under a machine model with sustained bandwidth \(\beta\) and arithmetic rate \(\rho\), define \(T_{\mathrm{move}}(n)=B(n)/\beta\) and \(T_{\mathrm{arith}}(n)=F(n)/\rho\). Data-movement dominance holds when \(T_{\mathrm{arith}}(n)=o(T_{\mathrm{move}}(n))\). In this regime, reducing oracle calls or flops need not reduce runtime unless it also reduces the transferred data or improves locality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data movement dominates when memory-transfer time asymptotically exceeds arithmetic time, so fewer flops or calls may not yield faster execution.
assumptions_latex: The machine parameters \(\beta\) and \(\rho\) are fixed for the compared implementation family.
Transferred bytes are counted across a specified memory boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Flop or query reductions alone need not reduce runtime when \(F(n)/\rho=o(B(n)/\beta)\).

notation.meaning: Bytes moved across the selected memory boundary.

children.title: Synchronization Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Coordination delays that dominate otherwise inexpensive local query work.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel speedup boundary caused by barriers or consistency waits on the critical execution path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a problem instance and stopping criterion. For execution on \(p\in\mathbb N\) workers, let \(T_p\) be total execution time and let \(s_{1,p},\ldots,s_{K(p),p}\ge0\) be durations of pairwise nonoverlapping synchronization waits that occur in order on the critical execution path. Then \(T_p\ge S_p:=\sum_{k=1}^{K(p)}s_{k,p}\). If there are constants \(s>0\) and \(p_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(S_p\ge s\) for every \(p\ge p_0\), then the speedup relative to one worker satisfies \(T_1/T_p\le T_1/s\) for \(p\ge p_0\), and therefore cannot grow proportionally to \(p\). Thus an iteration count that charges a synchronized parallel update as one unit can conceal a latency-dominated implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonoverlapping synchronization waits on the critical path impose a runtime lower bound; if that bound remains positive as workers are added, proportional speedup is impossible.
assumptions_latex: The synchronization waits are pairwise nonoverlapping and occur in order on the critical execution path.
Executions for different \(p\) use the same problem instance and stopping criterion.
\(T_1\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S_p=\sum_{k=1}^{K(p)}s_{k,p}\ge s>0\) eventually, then \(T_1/T_p\le T_1/s\) eventually.

notation.meaning: Duration of synchronization wait k on the critical path of the p-worker execution.
Accumulated nonoverlapping synchronization time on the critical path.
Total execution time on p workers.

children.title: Model-Comparison Failures
children.top_down_role: Invalid conclusions obtained by comparing results under nonmatching interfaces, resources, or success criteria.

children.title: Bundled–Unbundled Query Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Joint and separate information responses are treated as equivalent units.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundled–Unbundled Query Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalid comparison between joint oracle responses and separately purchased information components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a bundled oracle return \(O_B(x)=(u_1(x),\ldots,u_m(x))\) in one call, while an unbundled model supplies each \(u_i(x)\) through a separate oracle \(O_i\). A one-call simulation of \(O_B\) by the unbundled model generally costs \(m\) calls, whereas simulating a selected \(O_i\) from \(O_B\) costs one bundled call but reveals additional information. Therefore the two query counts are comparable only after stating simulations in both directions and their overheads; identifying one bundled call with one component call can change both upper and lower complexity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A call returning several information components is not equivalent to one call returning a selected component unless simulation overhead and extra information are accounted for.
assumptions_latex: All component responses are evaluated at the same query point \(x\).
Algorithms may adapt future queries to all information revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bundled and unbundled query complexities require explicit directional simulation factors.

notation.meaning: Oracle returning all m information components jointly.

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports bundled-oracle simulation comparisons

children.title: Local–Global Information Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Complexity claims compare local responses with reusable global information.

knowledge_statements.title: Local–Global Information Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison boundary between pointwise oracle answers and reusable descriptions valid over an entire domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a local oracle answer \(O_{m loc}(x)\) only at the queried point \(x\in X\), and let a global oracle return an object \(G\) from which \(O_{m loc}(x)\) can be evaluated for every \(x\in X\) without further oracle calls. One global call simulates arbitrarily many local evaluations once \(G\) is obtained. Unless \(G\) can itself be reconstructed from at most \(k\) local calls for a stated finite \(k\), counting a global response and a local response as equal query units does not preserve oracle complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusable domain-wide information can answer arbitrarily many point queries, so it cannot be equated with one local response without a reverse simulation bound.
assumptions_latex: The global response \(G\) remains reusable throughout the computation.
Evaluating the encoded local response from \(G\) requires no further oracle access.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local and global query counts are incomparable without bounded simulations in the required directions.

notation.meaning: Information available only at the queried point x.
Reusable representation encoding responses over the domain.

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports local-versus-global oracle simulation

children.title: Success-Criterion Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Complexity claims target nonequivalent notions of accuracy, probability, or certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Success-Criterion Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for comparing complexities stated under inequivalent accuracy, probability, or certification requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1(x,I,\varepsilon,\delta)\) and \(S_2(x,I,\varepsilon,\delta)\) be two success predicates for output \(x\) on instance \(I\). Complexity bounds under these criteria are directly comparable only when a uniform implication or reduction is stated: for example, \(S_1(x,I,\varepsilon,\delta)\Rightarrow S_2(x,I,\phi(\varepsilon),\psi(\delta))\), with the conversion functions and added resource cost explicit. Without such a relation, expected error, high-probability error, stationarity, objective gap, distance to a solution set, and possession of a verifiable certificate define potentially nonequivalent tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity bounds cannot be compared directly when their accuracy, probability, or certification goals differ without an explicit criterion conversion.
assumptions_latex: Both predicates are defined on the same stated instance class.
Any randomized guarantee specifies the probability space and failure parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid comparison requires an explicit reduction between \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) and its resource overhead.

notation.meaning: Success predicate j at accuracy epsilon and failure level delta.

children.title: Precision-Regime Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Exact, weak, approximate, and finite-precision access models are conflated.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Regime Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of comparisons that silently identify exact, approximate, weak, or finite-precision oracle access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O^{m ex}\) return an exact response, let \(O^{\eta}\) return a response within tolerance \(\eta\), and let \(O^{b}\) return a \(b\)-bit encoded response. Their query complexities are comparable only after specifying simulations that map responses and precision parameters between models, together with query and computational overhead. In particular, an exact call cannot generally be simulated by a fixed number of calls to \(O^{\eta}\) or \(O^{b}\) uniformly over arbitrarily small target error. Conversely, an exact response may contain strictly more information than any fixed-precision response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact, approximate, and finite-precision calls are not interchangeable unless precision conversion, simulation overhead, and attainable error are explicitly controlled.
assumptions_latex: Approximation error is measured in a specified metric or residual.
Finite-precision encoding and rounding conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complexity comparisons across precision regimes require explicit precision-dependent simulations.

notation.meaning: Oracle returning a b-bit encoded response.

children.title: Computational Resource Conflation
children.top_down_role: Distinct resource measures are treated as interchangeable.

children.title: Iteration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity accounting based on outer computational rounds or state transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case count of algorithmic update rounds needed to meet a fixed success criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an instance class \(\mathcal I\), an algorithm \(A\) producing iterates \((x_k(I))_{k\ge0}\), an accuracy parameter \(\varepsilon>0\), and a failure parameter \(\delta\in[0,1)\). Let \(\operatorname{Succ}_A(k,I,\varepsilon,\delta)\) denote the stated success guarantee after \(k\) iterations; for a randomized algorithm this statement includes probability at least \(1-\delta\), while for a deterministic algorithm it is an ordinary predicate. Define
\[K_A(\varepsilon,\delta)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:\operatorname{Succ}_A(k,I,\varepsilon,\delta)\}.\]
The infimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\). One iteration is the update round specified by \(A\), which may contain zero, one, or multiple oracle calls and arbitrary local or distributed work. Consequently, iteration complexity implies neither query complexity nor runtime complexity without corresponding per-iteration resource bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration complexity is the worst-case number of specified update rounds needed to obtain the declared deterministic or probabilistic success guarantee; it does not itself count calls or runtime.
assumptions_latex: The iterates \((x_k(I))_{k\ge0}\) and the unit called an iteration are specified by \(A\).
For randomized \(A\), \(\operatorname{Succ}_A\) identifies the probability space and requires success probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_A(\varepsilon,\delta)\) counts update rounds rather than oracle calls or execution time.

notation.meaning: Worst-case iteration count for algorithm A under the declared success guarantee.
Deterministic or probabilistic success statement after k iterations.

children.title: Query Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity accounting based on calls to the specified oracle interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Query Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case number of oracle transactions required to satisfy a specified success predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an instance class \(\mathcal I\), an oracle model \(\mathcal O\), an algorithm \(A\), a success predicate \(S(x,I,\varepsilon)\), and \(\delta\in[0,1)\). For each \(I\in\mathcal I\), let \(\omega\) denote the internal randomness of \(A\), let \(\tau_A(I,\omega)\) be its query-response transcript, and let \(X_A(I,\omega)\) be its output. Assume \(\Pr_\omega[S(X_A(I,\omega),I,\varepsilon)]\ge1-\delta\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\). If \(N_{\mathcal O}(\tau)\) counts charged calls under the declared bundling, precision, and adaptivity conventions, define the worst-case query complexity by
\[Q_A(\varepsilon,\delta)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\omega}N_{\mathcal O}(\tau_A(I,\omega)).\]
For deterministic \(A\), the essential supremum is omitted. If the stated success guarantee fails for some \(I\), set \(Q_A(\varepsilon,delta)=+\infty\). Query complexity excludes uncharged computation, communication, and variable call costs unless the oracle accounting rule explicitly charges them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case query complexity is the largest charged-call count, over instances and all non-null randomized executions, for an algorithm satisfying the declared success-probability requirement.
assumptions_latex: The oracle model specifies what one charged call returns and at what precision.
For randomized \(A\), the probability space governing \(\omega\) is specified.
The charging rule fixes bundling and adaptivity conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_A(\varepsilon,\delta)\) measures only charged oracle calls under the declared access and success conventions.

notation.meaning: Adaptive query-response transcript generated on instance I and random execution omega.
Number of calls charged by oracle model O in transcript tau.
Worst-case charged-call complexity at accuracy epsilon and failure level delta.
