children.title: Runtime Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity accounting for executable computational cost beyond query counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Runtime Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates charged computational cost from iteration and oracle-query counts in a specified computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a computational model \(M\) assigning costs to charged primitive operations, an input instance \(I\), an algorithm \(A\), and an accuracy parameter \(\varepsilon>0\). Let \(T_M(A,I,\varepsilon)\) be the total charged cost incurred before \(A\) returns an \(\varepsilon\)-acceptable output. If the execution completes \(K\) iterations and makes \(Q_j\) calls to oracle type \(j\), then bounds on \(K\) and \((Q_j)_j\) yield a runtime upper bound only when the model and implementation also provide uniform bounds on setup and termination costs, the number and cost of charged non-oracle operations associated with the counted iterations, and the cost of each oracle call. Without such conversion assumptions, equal iteration or query bounds do not imply comparable runtime bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Runtime is the total charged computational cost in a fixed model. Iteration and oracle-query bounds imply a runtime bound only when setup, non-oracle work, and oracle-call costs are uniformly controlled; otherwise equal count bounds need not give comparable runtime bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) specifies the charged primitive operations and their costs.
\(I\) belongs to the stated instance class.
\(A\) has a stated \(\varepsilon\)-acceptance criterion and stopping rule.
Setup, non-oracle work, and oracle implementations may depend on \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither \(K\) nor \((Q_j)_j\) alone yields a runtime bound for \(T_M(A,I,\varepsilon)\) without uniform bounds controlling all additional charged work.

notation.meaning: Total runtime cost charged to algorithm A on instance I at accuracy ε in model M.
Number of calls to oracle type j.

children.title: Resource-Conversion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on translating iteration counts or query counts into runtime claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Conversion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when bounds on one collection of computational resources can, and cannot, be converted into a bound on another resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an instance class and computational model, and let \(E\) be the set of admissible algorithm executions. For each \(e\in E\), let \(R(e)=(R_1(e),\ldots,R_m(e))\in[0,\infty)^m\) be the vector of source-resource costs and let \(S(e)\in[0,\infty)\) be the target-resource cost. A uniform conversion is a finite-valued, coordinatewise nondecreasing function \(F:[0,\infty)^m\to[0,\infty)\) justified by a specified simulation or implementation and satisfying \(S(e)\le F(R(e))\) for every \(e\in E\). An affine conversion is the special case \(F(r)=c_0+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i r_i\) with finite coefficients \(c_i\ge0\). If there is a finite vector \(r\in[0,\infty)^m\) for which \(S(e)\) is unbounded over executions satisfying \(R(e)\le r\) coordinatewise, then no such uniform conversion exists. Thus resource counts cannot be converted merely by identifying their units; a uniform implementation or simulation bound is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource conversion is a uniform bound on the target cost as a nondecreasing function of all source-resource costs. Affine conversion is only one special form. If target cost is unbounded while every source counter remains bounded, no uniform conversion exists, so merely matching resource labels or counts is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is the set of admissible executions over a fixed instance class and computational model.
\(R_i(e)\ge0\) and \(S(e)\ge0\) are resource costs measured for the same execution \(e\in E\).
A conversion bound must hold uniformly for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some finite \(r\in[0,\infty)^m\) satisfies \(\sup\{S(e):e\in E,\ R(e)\le r\}=\infty\), then no finite-valued coordinatewise nondecreasing \(F\) can satisfy \(S(e)\le F(R(e))\) for all \(e\in E\).

notation.meaning: Set of admissible executions in the fixed instance class and computational model.
Cost of source resource i in execution e.
Nonnegative coefficient in the special affine conversion.
